In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment. To proceed:

On this Thursday, the first of the month of Rajab in the year (1416 AH), we meet with our brothers in the session called "The Open Door Session," and this is the one hundred and ninth session.

At the end of the last session we completed the tafsir of Juz' 'Amma, from Surah an-Naba', and we decided to return and begin the tafsir of the surahs of al-Mufassal (the later short surahs of the Qur'an), which begin from Surah Qaf according to some scholars, or from Surah al-Hujurat according to others.

We will discuss Surah al-Hujurat because of the great and beneficial etiquettes it contains, which Allah began with His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ [al-Hujurat 1].

Know that when Allah begins an address with His saying ﴿O you who have believed﴾, then, as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "It is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from, so give it your hearing and listen to it, for in it there is good."[[Narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Tafsir (50) as a mawquf report from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]] When Allah opens an address with ﴿O you who have believed﴾, this indicates that adhering to what one is addressed with is among the requirements of faith, and that opposing it is a deficiency in faith.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾. It has been said that the meaning of ﴿do not put [yourselves]﴾ is: do not advance ahead of Allah and His Messenger, meaning do not precede Allah and His Messenger with a statement or an action. It has also been said that the meaning is: do not put anything before Allah and His Messenger. Both meanings converge in one direction, and the meaning is: do not precede Allah and His Messenger with a saying or a deed. Examples of this have occurred. Among them is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not precede Ramadan by fasting a day or two days,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1914) and Muslim (1082/21), from Abu Hurairah.]] because one who goes ahead of Ramadan by fasting a day or two is as if he has put himself before Allah and His Messenger, starting the fast before its time has come. For this reason 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: "Whoever fasts the day about which there is doubt has disobeyed Abu al-Qasim ﷺ."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2334) and al-Tirmidhi (686), the wording being his, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir.]]

Among it, that is, among putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger, is innovation (bid'ah) in all its types, for it is putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger, indeed it is the most severe form of advancing. This is because the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: "Hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided Caliphs after me, and beware of newly invented matters,"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4607) and al-Tirmidhi (2676), from al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah.]] and he informed that "every innovation is misguidance," and the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him spoke the truth. The reality of the innovator's condition is that he corrects what Allah and His Messenger left out, which he claims is good, as if he were saying that the Sharia was not complete, and that he has completed it with the innovation he brought. This is completely contradictory to the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3]. It is said to this man who innovated: Is this which you have done a perfection of the religion?

If he says, "Yes," then his statement entails denying the saying of Allah, ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion﴾. If he says, "It is not a perfection of the religion," we say: then it is a deficiency, for Allah says: ﴿So what is there after the truth except error?﴾ [Yunus 32]. Thus innovation, just as it is misguidance in itself, in reality also contains a slander against the religion of Allah, claiming it is deficient, and that this innovator has completed it with what he claims is from the Sharia of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

So all innovators have put themselves before Allah and His Messenger and have not heeded this prohibition, even if their intention is good; their action is misguidance. One may be rewarded for the goodness of his intention, but he will be burdened for the evil of his action. For this reason every innovator who knows that he is upon an innovation must repent from it, return to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and adhere to the Sunnah of the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided Caliphs after him.

Innovation has many types: innovations in belief ('aqidah), innovations in statements, and innovations in actions.

As for innovations in belief, they revolve around two things: either tamthil (likening Allah to creation) or ta'til (denying Allah's attributes).

Tamthil: that one affirms the attributes of Allah but in a manner of likeness to creation. This is an innovation, because it was not the way of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, nor of his rightly-guided Caliphs, so it is an innovation. For example, one affirms that Allah has a face and makes it like the faces of created beings, or that Allah has a hand and makes it like the hands of created beings, and so on. These innovators are undoubtedly in error, and their innovation is a denial of the saying of Allah, ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura 11], and of His saying, ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas 4], and of His saying, ﴿Do you know of any equal to Him?﴾ [Maryam 65].

As for ta'til, it is the opposite of this: ta'til is denying what Allah has described Himself with. If the denial is a denial of rejection and denial, it is kufr (disbelief). If it is denial by interpretation, it is tahrif (distortion), and it is not kufr if the wording admits it. If the wording does not admit it, there is no difference between it and the denial of rejection. For example, if a person says that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched﴾ [al-Ma'idah 64], and by the two hands is meant a blessing, the blessing of religion and the blessing of this world, or the blessing of this world and the blessing of the Hereafter. This is distortion, because blessings are not one, nor a thousand, nor millions: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [an-Nahl 18]. So blessings are not two, neither by genus nor by type. This would be distortion and innovation, because it contradicts what was received by the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and his companions, and the imams of guidance after them. This is an innovation in belief.

Innovation in statements: like those who innovate glorifications (tasbihat), or declarations of La ilaha illa Allah (tahlilat), or takbirs that the Sunnah has not transmitted, or who innovate supplications that the Sunnah has not transmitted and which are not among the permissible supplications.

As for innovations in actions, likewise, such as those who clap during remembrance of Allah, or who sway their heads during recitation, or similar kinds of innovation. Also those who rub themselves against the Ka'bah other than the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner; also those who rub themselves against the chamber of the Prophet ﷺ, the chamber of his noble grave; also those who rub themselves against the pulpit which is said to be the pulpit of the Prophet ﷺ in the Prophet's Mosque; also those who rub themselves against the walls of the cemetery of al-Baqi' or other than that.

In sum: innovations are many: those in belief, those in statements, and those in actions. All of them are among putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger, and all of them are disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. Allah says: ﴿Do not put [yourselves] before Allah and His Messenger﴾, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, says: "Beware of newly invented matters."

Among innovations is what is done in Rajab, such as the Salat ar-Raghaib, which is prayed on the night of the first Friday of the month of Rajab, and it is one thousand rak'ahs by which they worship Allah. This is an innovation that only increases them in distance from Allah, because whoever draws near to Allah by what He has not legislated is an innovator and astray, and Allah does not accept his worship. This is because of what is established in the Two Sahihs and others from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from 'A'ishah.]]

Among putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger is that a person says a statement by which he judges among the servants of Allah, or concerning the servants of Allah, which is not from the Sharia of Allah, such as saying: "This is haram, this is halal, this is obligatory, this is recommended," without evidence. This is among putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger. Whoever has said a statement and it becomes clear to him that he was mistaken in it must return to the truth, even if the statement has spread among people, become widely known, and been acted upon by some people. It is obligatory for him to return, and to announce his return as well, just as he announced his opposition, for which he may be excused if it arose from ijtihad (independent reasoning). The obligation is to return to the truth, and if a person persists in opposing the truth, he has put himself before Allah and His Messenger.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾. This is a generalization after a specification, because putting oneself before Allah and His Messenger contradicts taqwa, but He specified it and placed it first because of its importance. Then He said: ﴿And fear Allah﴾, meaning take a shield against the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is not realized except when a person performs the commands and abandons the prohibitions: performing the commands drawing near to Allah and out of love for His reward, and abandoning the prohibitions out of fear of the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Among people is one who, when told, "Fear Allah," is seized by pride in sin, becomes arrogant within himself, goes to excess in sin, his veins swell, and he says: "Someone like me is told, 'Fear Allah'?!" The wretched one does not know that Allah addressed one who is more noble than him, and who is the most God-fearing of the servants of Allah, and commanded him with taqwa. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ahzab 1], and in the same surah Allah says: ﴿And you were concealing within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. And who is not deserving of being commanded to fear Allah? Each one of us deserves to be commanded to fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is obligatory that when someone is told, "Fear Allah," he increase in fear of Allah, reconsider himself, and look at what he has been commanded. He has not been commanded to fear so-and-so and so-and-so; rather he has been commanded to fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

If we interpret taqwa in this way, namely as taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by performing His commands out of drawing near to Him and love for His reward, and abandoning His prohibitions out of fear of His punishment, then any person who abandons an obligation has not feared Allah, and has diminished his taqwa to the degree of the violation that occurred from him. Thus abandoning the prayer, for example, eliminates taqwa entirely, because one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever, as the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, and the sayings of the companions indicate. Some scholars have even related the consensus of the companions that one who abandons the prayer is a disbeliever in a kufr that removes him from the religion. Among them is the well-known Successor 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: "The companions of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, did not consider any of the deeds whose abandonment is kufr to be kufr except the prayer."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2622) from 'Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, who said: The companions of Muhammad...]] Likewise Ishaq ibn Rahawayh related their consensus. No companion is authentically reported to have said that one who abandons the prayer is in Paradise, or that he is a believer, or anything similar. Thus the violation of taqwa varies: its violation may be kufr, and it may be less than that. The adulterer has not feared Allah, because he committed adultery, opposing the command of Allah and disobeying Him. The thief has not feared Allah; the drinker of wine has not feared Allah; the one who is undutiful to his parents has not feared Allah; the one who severs the ties of kinship has not feared Allah. Examples of this are many. So His saying, ﴿And fear Allah﴾, is a general and comprehensive word that encompasses the entire Sharia.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ This sentence is a warning to us not to fall into what He has forbidden us of putting ourselves before Allah and His Messenger, or to oppose His command to fear Him. ﴿Hearing﴾ means: hearing of what you say. ﴿Knowing﴾ means: knowing of what you say and what you do. Knowledge is more comprehensive and general, since hearing relates to what is heard, while knowledge relates to what is known, and Allah, exalted is He, encompasses all things in knowledge: ﴿Nothing is hidden from Him on the earth or in the sky﴾ [Ali 'Imran 5].

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, say: the hearing with which our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is described is divided into two types: hearing of perception (sam' idrak) and hearing of response (sam' ijabah).

The meaning of hearing of perception is that Allah hears every sound, whether hidden or manifest, so much so that He, Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Allah has already heard the statement of the woman who is pleading with you concerning her husband and complaining to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual dialogue. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ [al-Mujadilah 1]. 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Praise be to Allah, Who has encompassed the hearing of all voices. I was in the chamber" (meaning the chamber of the Prophet ﷺ) "and the woman was pleading with him, and he was conversing with her, and some of her speech was hidden from me."[[Narrated by al-Nasa'i (3460) and Ibn Majah (188) from 'A'ishah.]] Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He heard, and He hears all that passed between this woman and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. To this we say: it is hearing of perception.

Then hearing of perception may be intended to express comprehensiveness and encompassing, it may be intended as a threat, and it may be intended as support. These are three types: it is intended to express comprehensiveness and encompassing, like this verse.

It may be intended as a threat, like His saying: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich. We will record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, 'Taste the punishment of the burning.'"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 181]. Observe how He said, ﴿We will record what they have said﴾ when they described Allah with deficiency, before He said, ﴿and their killing of the prophets﴾, which indicates that describing Allah with deficiency is greater than killing the prophets. This is hearing intended as what? A threat.

The third: hearing intended as support, such as the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46]. The meaning of hearing here is support: "I hear, so I support you; I hear what you say and what is said to you both."

As for hearing of response, its meaning is that Allah responds to whoever calls upon Him, and from it is the saying of Ibrahim: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], meaning Responder to supplication. And from it is the saying of the one praying: "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him), meaning He responds to him, responds to whoever praises Him by rewarding him. We do not know whether we realize the meaning of what we say in our prayers, or whether we say it as an act of worship without knowing its meaning. When you say "Allahu Akbar" at the opening takbir, it means He is greater than everything, Mighty and Majestic, and we do not encompass that, because He is greater than our minds can encompass. When we say "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah," it means Allah responds to whoever praises Him. The meaning is not merely that He hears him, because Allah hears whoever praises Him and whoever does not praise Him when he speaks; rather, the meaning is that He responds to whoever praises Him with reward. This hearing requires responding to whoever calls upon Him.

As for His saying, ﴿Knowing﴾, it means that He possesses vast knowledge. Allah says: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [at-Talaq 12].

When you believe, brother, that Allah is Hearing and that Allah is Knowing, is it possible, while you have sound reason, that you would say what does not please Him? No; because He hears. It is not fitting for you to make Allah hear from you what He does not like; make Him hear what He loves and is pleased with. If you truly believe that Allah is Hearing, I think that if your father forbade you from saying something, would you dare to let him hear what he forbade you from? No.

Allah is greater and more majestic. So beware of making Allah hear from you what He does not approve. If you believe that He knows everything, and this is more general than hearing, since it includes speech, action, and the inner thoughts of the soul, even what your self whispers is known to Him, Mighty and Majestic. Having known this, could you do something that does not please Him? No.

For the purpose of Allah informing us that He is Knowing of all things is not merely that we know this and believe it.

The purpose here is one thing, and there is another purpose, which is the fruit and result that follows from our knowledge that Allah is All-Knowing of everything. If we know that He is All-Knowing of everything, would we say what He does not approve of? No, because He will know it. If we know that He is All-Knowing of everything, would we hold a belief He does not approve of? No, because we know that He knows what is in our hearts. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is within your souls, so beware of Him﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:235]. Rather, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal 8:24], meaning He comes between you and your heart.

So in any case, O brothers, it is obligatory upon us that whenever a name of Allah or an attribute of Allah passes by us, we believe in this name and this attribute, and that we act upon what is the fruit of faith in this name or attribute.

I ask Allah the Exalted to grant us and you steadfastness in our religion and our worldly life, and to bestow upon us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 2:

We have discussed Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ [al-Hujurat 1]. This is a great etiquette that Allah the Exalted directed His servants to.

As for the second etiquette, it is in His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive﴾ [al-Hujurat 2].

The first verse contains the prohibition of putting oneself forward before Allah and His Messenger in anything, whether in statements, actions, or otherwise. We have already explained what the verse indicates. The second verse concerns raising the voice, even if there is no putting forward in rulings, such as declaring something lawful, unlawful, or obligatory. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾. So if the Prophet (ﷺ) addresses you in a certain voice, lower your voice below his voice, and if he raises his voice, raise yours, but it must remain below the voice of the Messenger (peace be upon him). For this reason He said: ﴿Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet﴾, and ﴿do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾. That is, do not call out to him in a raised voice as some of you call out to others. Rather, your speech should be delivered with courtesy, honor, and veneration befitting him (ﷺ and his family). This is like His words: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾ [an-Nur 63]. That is, when he calls you to something, do not make his call like the call of one of you to another. If you wish, you may respond, and if you wish, you may not. Rather, responding is obligatory upon you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal 24]. Here He said: ﴿and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another﴾.

Likewise, do not address him with what you address one another. So do not say, "O Muhammad!" but say, "O Messenger of Allah!" or "O Prophet of Allah!" and the like. ﴿and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive﴾. That is, out of fear that your deeds may be nullified. In other words, we have only forbidden you from raising your voices above his voice and from speaking loudly to him as some of you speak loudly to others, out of fear that your deeds will be nullified while you do not perceive it. This indicates that one who raises his voice above the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ), or speaks loudly to him in the way he speaks loudly to some people, may have his deeds nullified without his realizing it, because this may produce in a person's heart contempt for the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And contempt for the Messenger is apostasy (riddah, leaving Islam), which necessitates the nullification of deeds.

When this verse was revealed, Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas (may Allah be pleased with him) had a loud voice, and he was one of the orators of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). When this verse was revealed, he withdrew to his house and stopped attending the gatherings of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger missed him and asked about him, and they informed him that he had been in his house since the verse was revealed. So the Messenger sent someone to him to ask about him. Thabit said: "Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, and do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, lest your deeds be nullified while you do not perceive﴾, and I have feared that my deeds have been nullified, and that I am among the people of the Fire." The Prophet (ﷺ) gave an order, and Thabit was summoned. He came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) informed him that he was among the people of Paradise, and said: "Are you not pleased to live praiseworthy, to be killed as a martyr, and to enter Paradise?" He said: "Yes, I am pleased."[[Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (7167), al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (5105), and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (1310), from the hadith of Thabit ibn Qays.]] Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him) was then killed as a martyr at the Battle of Yamama, lived praiseworthy, and was to enter Paradise by the testimony of the Messenger (peace be upon him). For this reason, Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him) is one of those for whom it is testified specifically that he is among the people of Paradise. This is because every person for whom the Prophet (ﷺ) testifies that he is in Paradise is in Paradise, and every person for whom he testifies that he is in the Fire is in the Fire. As for one for whom the Messenger has not testified, we testify in general terms: we say, every believer is in Paradise and every disbeliever is in the Fire, and we do not testify for a specific person that he is among the people of the Fire or among the people of Paradise, except for what Allah and His Messenger have testified.

* In this noble verse there is a clarification of the veneration of the Messenger (ﷺ), that it is not permissible for a person to speak to him loudly as he speaks to the rest of people, and that it is not permissible for him to raise his voice above the voice of the Messenger (peace be upon him). When this verse was revealed, the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) adopted this etiquette so thoroughly that some of them would speak to him in a low whisper, and the Messenger would not understand what they said in their whisper until he asked them to repeat it.

* In this verse there is evidence that whoever treats the command of the Messenger (peace be upon him) with contempt, his deeds are nullified, because contempt for the Messenger (peace be upon him) is apostasy, and mocking him is apostasy. As Allah the Exalted said about the hypocrites who used to mock the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿If you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing"﴾ [at-Tawbah 65]. They used to say: "We have never seen the likes of these reciters of ours, meaning the Messenger (ﷺ) and his Companions. They have the greatest appetites (meaning they are the most gluttonous), and they are the most cowardly at the time of encounter, and the most lying in their tongues."[[See Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan), Hajr edition (11/543).]]

So Allah revealed this verse. When the Messenger (peace be upon him) asked them about that, they said: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾, meaning we were speaking words we did not intend, but only to cut off the path for ourselves. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [at-Tawbah 65-66].

For this reason, the correct position is that whoever curses the Messenger (peace be upon him) is a disbeliever and an apostate. If he repents, we accept his repentance, but we do not lift the death penalty from him; rather, we execute him in fulfillment of the right of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). If we execute him after his sincere and true repentance, we pray over him just as we pray over the rest of the Muslims who repent from disbelief or from sins.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 49, verse 3:

Then Allah, the Exalted, praised those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ), saying: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah—those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety. For them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ [al-Hujurat 3] After He had forbidden raising one's voice above his voice, and speaking loudly to him as some of you speak loudly to one another, He praised those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah. That is, they lower them and speak with courtesy, without disturbance, clamour, or raising their voices. Rather, they speak with courtesy and humility. Allah said: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety.﴾ He repeated the demonstrative, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah—those ones (ulā'ika, a demonstrative noun) who...﴾, to magnify their status and elevate their rank. Ulā' is a demonstrative noun indicating distance, and this is because of the高 elevation of their rank. Otherwise, the sentence would be complete if He had said: "Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah are those whose hearts Allah has tested for piety." But He brought the demonstrative to make clear the exaltedness and loftiness of their rank.

﴿Allah has tested their hearts﴾. The scholars said: its meaning is that He purified them for piety, so their hearts were filled with the piety of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason they adopted the courtesy that Allah directed them to, so they lowered their voices in the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Their reward: ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward.﴾ Forgiveness from Allah for their sins, and a great reward for their righteous deeds. In this verse there is an indication that righteousness is the righteousness of the heart, as shown by His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety.﴾ As the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the authentic hadith: "Piety is here," and he pointed to his chest [[Recorded by Muslim (2564/32) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], which is the seat of the heart, three times: "Piety is here, piety is here, piety is here." There is no doubt that piety is the piety of the heart. As for the piety of the limbs, which is the correction of outward action, this may occur even among the hypocrites: ﴿When you see them, their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ [al-Munafiqun 4]. But the discussion is about the piety of the heart, by which righteousness comes about. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant us and you that.

﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety.﴾ Some people commit sins, and when you disapprove of them, they say: "Piety is here," as if they are purifying themselves, while they persist in disobeying Allah. We say to him with complete ease: If what is here were pious, the limbs would be pious, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52) and Muslim (1599/107) from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]]. You meet a person who persists in some sin, such as letting his garment hang below the ankles, shaving his beard, or smoking tobacco, and you forbid him and warn him of Allah's punishment, and he says to you: "Piety is here." The answer is that we say: If there were piety in what is here, then what is here would be pious. The proof is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Verily, it is the heart."

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who call out to you from behind the chambers—most of them do not use their reason﴾ [al-Hujurat 4]. This verse refers to a people who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and with them were some uncouth people who did not appreciate matters in their proper measure. They began calling out to the Prophet (ﷺ) from behind his chambers, that is, the chambers of his wives, raising their voices in doing so, wanting the Prophet (ﷺ) to come out to them. Allah says about these people: ﴿most of them do not use their reason﴾, meaning: they have no 'aql (reason). The 'aql meant here is 'aql of rushd (sound judgment), because 'aql is of two kinds: 'aql of rushd (sound judgment) and 'aql of taklif (moral accountability).

The opposite of 'aql of rushd is safah (foolishness), and the opposite of 'aql of taklif is madness (junun). So, for example, if we say: "It is a condition for the validity of wudu' that the one performing it be 'aqil (sane) and mumayyiz (discerning)," then the 'aql meant here is 'aql of taklif. And if we say: "It is a condition for disposing of wealth that the one disposing be 'aqil," meaning 'aql of rushd, one who handles affairs well.

So what is meant by His statement here, ﴿most of them do not use their reason﴾, is: they do not have 'aql of rushd. For if they lacked 'aql of taklif, there would be no blame or censure upon them, since the madman, who lacks reason, is not subject to blame or censure. This is clear.

His statement ﴿most of them do not use their reason﴾ implies that some of them do have reason, and that there was no raising of voices from them, but rather that they were courteous toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on Surah al-Hujurat (49), verse 5:

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And if they had patience until you come out to them, it would have been better for them﴾ [al-Hujurat 5]. That is, out of your house, and you speak to them about what they want. ﴿It would have been better for them.﴾ Better for them in what? Better for them in that they would have observed good manners with the Prophet ﷺ, and their need would have been fulfilled, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never had anyone come to him with a need without fulfilling it, if he was able to. He was the most deserving of people of the words of the poet:

He never said "No" except in his tashahhud,
and were it not for the tashahhud, his "no" would have been "yes."

﴿And if they had patience until you come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ In the Exalted's words ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful⁠﴾ is an indication that Allah has forgiven them and shown them mercy. This is from His generosity, may He be exalted, that He forgives and shows mercy. Allah the Exalted has informed us in His Book: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa 48]. That is, what is other than shirk. So whoever commits a sin less than shirk, however great, is under the will of Allah: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He forgives him, as long as he does not repent. If he repents, there is no punishment, due to the Exalted's words: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse—and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation. Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Furqan 68–70].

Here we said: the verse indicates that Allah has forgiven them and shown them mercy. From where do we derive this indication? We derive it from the fact that Allah concluded the verse with His words: ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and this indicates that He has forgiven them and shown them mercy. For this reason the scholars said regarding the Exalted's words about those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth in corruption, that their recompense is ﴿that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is a disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. Except for those who repent before you gain power over them; so know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33–34]. The scholars derived from this verse that these corrupters who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, if they repent before they are overpowered, the punishment is dropped from them, and they used as evidence that Allah concluded the verse with His words: ﴿So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning He has forgiven them and shown them mercy. This is a subtle point that the student of knowledge should pay attention to in the verses: that concluding a verse after mentioning a ruling is evidence of what these names with which the verse is concluded require.

For this reason a man recited the Exalted's words: "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands as recompense for what they earned as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," and a Bedouin who was with him heard him and said: "Repeat the verse." He repeated it, saying: "And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands as recompense for what they earned as a punishment from Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." He said: "Repeat the verse." He repeated it, and [the Bedouin] said: ﴿And the thief, male and female, cut off their hands as recompense for what they earned, as a punishment from Allah; and Allah is Mighty and Wise⁠﴾ [al-Ma'idah 38]. He said: "Now you are right," that is, "Now you have got it right." Then he gave the reason, saying: "Because if He had forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off the hand. Forgiveness and mercy are not compatible with amputation, but He is Mighty and Wise, so He cut it off."

So reflect on this understanding, for it is very beneficial to you.

The point here is that the Exalted's words ﴿And if they had patience until you come out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Hujurat 5] show that the verse indicates Allah has forgiven them and shown them mercy.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 6–8 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 6].

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When you hear Allah say, ﴿O you who have believed,﴾ then lend it your hearing (i.e., listen to it), for it is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Recorded by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50) as a mawquf report from Ibn Mas'ud.]] This is because it is an address with the most noble of descriptions, which is faith (iman): ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾.

So who is the fasiq (deviator)? The fasiq is one who has deviated in his religion and his manliness (muruwwah). Its opposite is the 'adl (upright person), who is one who is steadfast in his religion and his manliness, and this is the opposite of the fasiq. If a deviator comes to us, one who has deviated in his religion and his manliness, meaning that he persists in sins and abandons obligations, yet he has not reached the level of disbelief; or one who has deviated in his manliness, who does not care about himself, walks among people with a frivolous gait, speaks with raised voice, carries the items of his household through the markets and the like, which contravenes manliness, then this, according to the scholars, is not upright.

In this verse Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿if a deviator brings a report﴾, a report, i.e., a news report, and he is a deviator. Let us apply this matter to reality: a man comes to us who shaves his beard. He who shaves his beard is a deviator. Why? Because he persists in disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Let the beards grow."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5893) and Muslim (259/52) from Ibn 'Umar.]] This man has not let his beard grow, rather he has shaved it, so this man is among the deviators, because he persists in disobedience. He brings us a report: shall we accept it? No. Shall we reject it? No. We do not accept it, because of the deviation that is in him; and we do not reject it, because it is possible that he is truthful. Therefore Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿verify it⦁﴾, and He did not say: reject it, nor did He say: accept it. Rather it is obligatory upon us to verify. In another reading: ﴿fa-tathabbatu﴾ (make certain), and both have closely similar meanings: that we seek certainty.

If someone says: then there is no benefit in his report, we say: No, rather there is benefit in his report: it stirs the soul so that we inquire and investigate, for had it not been for his report we would not have stirred at all. But when he brings the report we say: perhaps he is truthful, so we move, inquire and investigate. If reality bears witness to its truth, we accept it; otherwise we reject it.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾ indicate that if an upright person comes to us, we accept the report. But this has detail according to the scholars, as indicated by the Qur'an and the Sunnah. For example, testimony of adultery: if an upright man, steadfast in his religion and manliness, comes to us and testifies that so-and-so committed adultery, do we accept his testimony? No, even though he is upright. Rather we flog him eighty lashes, because he has slandered this innocent man with adultery, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient⦁﴾ [al-Nur 4]. So we flog him eighty lashes, and we never accept his testimony, and we judge him to be a deviator, even if he is upright, until he repents.

If two upright men testify against Zayd that he committed adultery, do we accept their testimony? No. Three? No. Four? Yes, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient⦁﴾, and He said: ﴿Why did they not produce for it four witnesses? So when they do not produce the witnesses, then those with Allah are the liars⦁﴾ [al-Nur 13]. Even if they are truthful: if three came to us whom we know to be trustworthy and upright and they testified to adultery against a person, then in the sight of Allah they are liars, not accepted; and as I told you, each one of them is flogged eighty lashes.

If a man came to us and testified against a person that he had stolen, do we accept his testimony? No, two men are necessary.

If a man came to us and testified that he saw the crescent of Ramadan, do we accept his testimony? Yes, we accept it, because the Sunnah has reported this. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The people sighted the crescent" — i.e., on the night of the thirtieth of Sha'ban — "so I informed the Prophet ﷺ that I had seen it, and he fasted and commanded the people to fast."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (2342) from Ibn 'Umar.]]

A man who had been wealthy but was struck by a calamity, then came asking for zakat, and brought a witness that he had been wealthy but had been struck by a calamity and became poor: do we accept the testimony of one? No. Do we accept the testimony of two? No. Three are necessary, because the Prophet ﷺ said to Qabisah: "Begging is not permitted except for ..." and he mentioned among them: "a man who was struck by a calamity" — i.e., it destroyed his wealth — "and three of the wise ones from among his people testify that so-and-so was struck by a calamity, so begging becomes permissible for him,"[[Recorded by Muslim (1044/109) from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq.]] "three of the wise ones" meaning: of the people of intellect.

So the summary: what is our position regarding the report of the deviator? Suspension until the matter is clarified. As for the non-deviator, there is detail: we may accept only the testimony of four, as in adultery, or three, as in the case of the man who was wealthy, then was struck by a calamity, then came asking for charity: we do not accept from him until three testify. Two are required where a person testifies to a hadd punishment for theft.

It is possible to accept: one man together with the oath of the claimant, as if a person claims against another that he owes him a thousand riyals, and we say to the claimant: bring evidence. He says: I have one man. If he brings the one man and swears with him, we rule in his favour according to what he claimed. On this basis, the report of the upright has detail as you have heard, and in matters too many to be mentioned in this context.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained the wisdom behind our verifying the report of the deviator, saying: ﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 6]. That is: We have commanded you to verify, out of dislike that you harm a people out of ignorance; for a person is hasty, and if he does not verify, he may transgress against another on the basis of the report he heard from the deviator, and he may come to hate him, and may speak about him in gatherings, and then afterwards, when it becomes clear that the report of the deviator was false, he becomes regretful for what he has done.

* In this verse there is evidence that a person is obligated to verify what he transmits of reports, especially with desire and partisanship. If a report about a person reaches you and you do not trust the word of the reporter, you must verify, and not be hasty in judgment, for you may be hasty and build upon this false report, and then regret afterwards. From this comes the warning against namimah (tale-bearing), which is conveying the words of people to one another in order to cause discord among them. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6056) and Muslim (105/169) from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] — i.e., one who carries tales. And it is authentically reported from him ﷺ that he passed by two graves being punished and said: "Indeed they are being punished, and they are not being punished for something great" — i.e., for a matter that was difficult for them — "as for one of them, he did not guard himself from urine" — or "did not purify himself from urine" or "did not clean himself of urine," [variant reports] — "and as for the other, he used to walk about with tale-bearing," walking among people carrying talk to others in order to spread discord among them. "Then he took a fresh palm frond, split it into two, and planted one on each grave." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, why have you done this?" He said: "Perhaps it will lighten their punishment as long as they do not dry out."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (216) and Muslim (292/111) from Ibn 'Abbas.]]

﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁﴾. Among this kind is what is attributed to some scholars of fatwas which they never spoke at all, or they spoke the opposite of what is transmitted from them. Some people may understand a word of a scholar in a sense other than the scholar intended, and a person may ask a scholar a question which the scholar understands differently from what the questioner has in mind, and then he answers according to what he understood; then this man comes and spreads this statement which is not correct. How many statements have been attributed to eminent scholars, yet had no basis! Therefore it is obligatory to verify what is transmitted from scholars or non-scholars, especially, as I said to you just now, especially in this age in which desires have multiplied, partisanship has multiplied, and people have come to walk as if in blindness.

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty. But Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it appealing in your hearts⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 7]. As you know, this verse came after the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁ And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Hujurat 6, 7].

The cause of what preceded was that the Prophet ﷺ had been informed about some people concerning matters that were not in them, so Allah the Exalted commanded verifying reports when they are brought by one whose uprightness is not known. It seems that some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wanted the Prophet ﷺ to punish those about whom he had been informed, but the Prophet ﷺ did not do so after the verse was revealed: ﴿If a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾.

But the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, which is His words: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾, i.e., it would be hard upon you, what you request from the Messenger ﷺ.

There are many examples of this. Among them: the Prophet ﷺ once led his Companions in Ramadan in the night prayer; he departed when some of the night remained, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had extended for us the rest of our night" — i.e., they asked him to stand with them the whole night — but he ﷺ said to them: "Whoever stands with the imam until he departs, a night's standing is written for him,"[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (1375) and al-Tirmidhi (806) from Abu Dhar.]] and he did not agree with their request, because of the difficulty and hardship in it.

Among them: some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ inquired about his deeds in private — i.e., what was not apparent to people — which are the acts of worship he performed in his house, and they considered them little, and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been forgiven his past and future sins," meaning: as for us, that is not for us. One of them said: "I will fast and not break my fast." The second said: "I will stand and not sleep." The third said: "And I will not marry women." When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "As for me, I fast and break my fast, I stand and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401/5) from Anas ibn Malik.]] He thus warned them against doing deeds that would be hard for them.

Also among this is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that "it reached the Prophet ﷺ that he had said: 'I will fast the day and stand in prayer the night as long as I live.' The Prophet ﷺ summoned him and said: 'Did you say this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You cannot bear that.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1976) and Muslim (1159/181) from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr.]] Then he guided him to what was better and easier.

The summary: among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, there are those with lofty resolve, but the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, did not obey them in much of the matter, because that would have been hard upon them had he obeyed them.

Then He said: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾.

Someone may say: what is the connection between His words, ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, and His words, ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾?

The answer: you obey him — i.e., the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace — in what goes against your wishes, because Allah has endeared the faith to you, so you prefer obedience to the Prophet ﷺ in what contradicts you; because Allah has endeared the faith to you and made it appealing in your hearts. This is a corrective exception of the most eloquent kind; meaning: but if the Prophet ﷺ opposes you in much of what you want, you will not hate that, nor will you oppose him, nor will you bear ill will toward the Messenger ﷺ because of it. ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, i.e., made it beloved in your hearts, ﴿and made it appealing in your hearts﴾, meaning: He made you love it, and made it appealing in your hearts such that you do not abandon it after you have acted upon it. This is because a person's doing a thing out of love may be a passing love, but when the thing is made attractive to him, the love becomes firm and lasting. Therefore He said: ﴿endeared to you the faith﴾, and this is in the heart; and ﴿made it appealing in your hearts﴾ also in the heart. But when the beloved thing is made attractive to a person, he persists in it and remains steadfast upon it.

﴿And He has made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to you﴾: He made hateful to you disbelief, which is the opposite of faith; defiance, which is the opposite of steadfastness; and disobedience, which is the opposite of perfection. This is a descent from the highest to what is below it: disbelief is greater than defiance, and defiance is greater than disobedience. Disbelief is leaving Islam entirely, and it has well-known causes in the books of the scholars, which the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned in the chapter on the rulings of the apostate. As for defiance, it is less than disbelief, but it is the commission of a major sin: that a person commits a major sin and does not repent from it, such as adultery, drinking wine, theft, slander, and the like. Disobedience is below this, and disobedience means minor sins, which are expiated by good deeds, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, so long as major sins are avoided."[[Recorded by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah.]] So the sincere believers, Allah has endeared the faith to them, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to them. We ask Allah to make us among them.

﴿Those are the rightly guided⦁﴾. "Those" refers to those whom Allah has endeared the faith to, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to.

﴿Those are the rightly guided﴾, meaning: those who have taken the path of rectitude (rushd). Rushd in origin means good conduct, and it varies in each context. Rushd in wealth is that a person manages it well and does not spend it on what is not beneficial.

Rushd in guardianship of marriage, for example, is that the guardian knows what is suitable (kafa'ah) and the interests of the marriage.

Rushd in religion is steadfastness upon the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Those whom Allah has endeared the faith to and made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to, are the rightly guided.

And here you find all these actions attributed to Allah: He endeared — who? He made it appealing — Allah. He made hateful — Allah, Mighty and Majestic...

Thus He said after it: ﴿Grace from Allah﴾, meaning: Allah has bestowed upon you grace, that is, a favour from Him, and it is not by your own earning, but it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And so that it may be known that Allah, the Exalted, knows best where to place His message, and knows best where to place faith in a person. Whoever Allah knows to have good intention, good purpose and sincerity, faith is made beloved to him, He adorns it in his heart, and He makes disbelief, wickedness and disobedience hateful to him. And whoever Allah does not know to have that, then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5], and the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. So sins are a cause of opposition and disobedience. Those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour and blessed them with the blessing of religion are those who were granted success in the truth. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Grace from Allah and a blessing﴾, meaning: a bestowal of blessing from Him upon them.

Blessing is of two kinds: a blessing in this world and a blessing in the Hereafter.

As for the disbelievers, they are granted comfort in this world, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and luxury in which they were jubilant﴾ [al-Dukhan 25–27], meaning: enjoyment. So these, that is the disbelievers, have a blessing in this world, but in the Hereafter there awaits them punishment and curse, and we seek refuge with Allah.

As for the believer, he obtains both blessings, the blessing of this world and the blessing of the Hereafter, even if he is poor, sick, childless, or has no lineage; for he is in blessing, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl 97].

Here He said: ﴿Grace and blessing from Allah﴾. The intended blessing here is the blessing of religion, which is connected to the blessing of the Hereafter.

The summary regarding blessing is that there are two blessings: a general blessing for all creation – the disbeliever and the believer, the wicked and the obedient – and a specific blessing for the believer. This specific blessing is connected to the blessing of religion and of this world. As for the first, it is specific only to the blessing of this world, so that the proof may be established against the disbelievers.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. These are two of the names of Allah, which Allah always pairs together: knowledge and wisdom. He is All-Knowing of everything; Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Talaq 12], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman 34], and the Exalted said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am 59], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Ali 'Imran 5].

So the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, encompasses everything. When a person knows that the knowledge of Allah encompasses everything, even what he conceals in his heart, he fears, is awed, and flees to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He does not say a word that angers Allah, nor does he do an act that angers Allah, nor does he harbour a belief that angers Allah, for he knows that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that and nothing is hidden from Him.

As for the Wise, He is the possessor of perfect wisdom. Wisdom means that everything He decrees, may He be exalted, is in accordance with and conforms to the interests; there is nothing Allah decrees except that it is a great wisdom. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Far-reaching wisdom, but warnings do not avail﴾ [al-Qamar 5], and the Exalted said: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8], and the Exalted said: ﴿And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50]. This is the meaning of the Wise, that is, the possessor of perfect wisdom.

It has another meaning: the possessor of complete judgement. Allah, the Exalted, holds judgement, as He said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura 10], and the Exalted said: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Nisa' 59], and no one judges by his own desire: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to take us and you under His care with His mercy and pardon, and to make us among those who know and benefit from their knowledge; indeed, He is over all things competent.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 6–8 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 6].

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "When you hear Allah say, ﴿O you who have believed,﴾ then lend it your hearing (i.e., listen to it), for it is either good that you are commanded to do, or evil that you are forbidden from."[[Recorded by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Tafsir (50) as a mawquf report from Ibn Mas'ud.]] This is because it is an address with the most noble of descriptions, which is faith (iman): ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾.

So who is the fasiq (deviator)? The fasiq is one who has deviated in his religion and his manliness (muruwwah). Its opposite is the 'adl (upright person), who is one who is steadfast in his religion and his manliness, and this is the opposite of the fasiq. If a deviator comes to us, one who has deviated in his religion and his manliness, meaning that he persists in sins and abandons obligations, yet he has not reached the level of disbelief; or one who has deviated in his manliness, who does not care about himself, walks among people with a frivolous gait, speaks with raised voice, carries the items of his household through the markets and the like, which contravenes manliness, then this, according to the scholars, is not upright.

In this verse Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿if a deviator brings a report﴾, a report, i.e., a news report, and he is a deviator. Let us apply this matter to reality: a man comes to us who shaves his beard. He who shaves his beard is a deviator. Why? Because he persists in disobedience to Allah and His Messenger. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Let the beards grow."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5893) and Muslim (259/52) from Ibn 'Umar.]] This man has not let his beard grow, rather he has shaved it, so this man is among the deviators, because he persists in disobedience. He brings us a report: shall we accept it? No. Shall we reject it? No. We do not accept it, because of the deviation that is in him; and we do not reject it, because it is possible that he is truthful. Therefore Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿verify it⦁﴾, and He did not say: reject it, nor did He say: accept it. Rather it is obligatory upon us to verify. In another reading: ﴿fa-tathabbatu﴾ (make certain), and both have closely similar meanings: that we seek certainty.

If someone says: then there is no benefit in his report, we say: No, rather there is benefit in his report: it stirs the soul so that we inquire and investigate, for had it not been for his report we would not have stirred at all. But when he brings the report we say: perhaps he is truthful, so we move, inquire and investigate. If reality bears witness to its truth, we accept it; otherwise we reject it.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿if a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾ indicate that if an upright person comes to us, we accept the report. But this has detail according to the scholars, as indicated by the Qur'an and the Sunnah. For example, testimony of adultery: if an upright man, steadfast in his religion and manliness, comes to us and testifies that so-and-so committed adultery, do we accept his testimony? No, even though he is upright. Rather we flog him eighty lashes, because he has slandered this innocent man with adultery, and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient⦁﴾ [al-Nur 4]. So we flog him eighty lashes, and we never accept his testimony, and we judge him to be a deviator, even if he is upright, until he repents.

If two upright men testify against Zayd that he committed adultery, do we accept their testimony? No. Three? No. Four? Yes, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever after. And those are the defiantly disobedient⦁﴾, and He said: ﴿Why did they not produce for it four witnesses? So when they do not produce the witnesses, then those with Allah are the liars⦁﴾ [al-Nur 13]. Even if they are truthful: if three came to us whom we know to be trustworthy and upright and they testified to adultery against a person, then in the sight of Allah they are liars, not accepted; and as I told you, each one of them is flogged eighty lashes.

If a man came to us and testified against a person that he had stolen, do we accept his testimony? No, two men are necessary.

If a man came to us and testified that he saw the crescent of Ramadan, do we accept his testimony? Yes, we accept it, because the Sunnah has reported this. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The people sighted the crescent" — i.e., on the night of the thirtieth of Sha'ban — "so I informed the Prophet ﷺ that I had seen it, and he fasted and commanded the people to fast."[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (2342) from Ibn 'Umar.]]

A man who had been wealthy but was struck by a calamity, then came asking for zakat, and brought a witness that he had been wealthy but had been struck by a calamity and became poor: do we accept the testimony of one? No. Do we accept the testimony of two? No. Three are necessary, because the Prophet ﷺ said to Qabisah: "Begging is not permitted except for ..." and he mentioned among them: "a man who was struck by a calamity" — i.e., it destroyed his wealth — "and three of the wise ones from among his people testify that so-and-so was struck by a calamity, so begging becomes permissible for him,"[[Recorded by Muslim (1044/109) from Qabisah ibn Mukhariq.]] "three of the wise ones" meaning: of the people of intellect.

So the summary: what is our position regarding the report of the deviator? Suspension until the matter is clarified. As for the non-deviator, there is detail: we may accept only the testimony of four, as in adultery, or three, as in the case of the man who was wealthy, then was struck by a calamity, then came asking for charity: we do not accept from him until three testify. Two are required where a person testifies to a hadd punishment for theft.

It is possible to accept: one man together with the oath of the claimant, as if a person claims against another that he owes him a thousand riyals, and we say to the claimant: bring evidence. He says: I have one man. If he brings the one man and swears with him, we rule in his favour according to what he claimed. On this basis, the report of the upright has detail as you have heard, and in matters too many to be mentioned in this context.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained the wisdom behind our verifying the report of the deviator, saying: ﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 6]. That is: We have commanded you to verify, out of dislike that you harm a people out of ignorance; for a person is hasty, and if he does not verify, he may transgress against another on the basis of the report he heard from the deviator, and he may come to hate him, and may speak about him in gatherings, and then afterwards, when it becomes clear that the report of the deviator was false, he becomes regretful for what he has done.

* In this verse there is evidence that a person is obligated to verify what he transmits of reports, especially with desire and partisanship. If a report about a person reaches you and you do not trust the word of the reporter, you must verify, and not be hasty in judgment, for you may be hasty and build upon this false report, and then regret afterwards. ﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁﴾. Among this kind is what is attributed to some scholars of fatwas which they never spoke at all, or they spoke the opposite of what is transmitted from them. Some people may understand a word of a scholar in a sense other than the scholar intended, and a person may ask a scholar a question which the scholar understands differently from what the questioner has in mind, and then he answers according to what he understood; then this man comes and spreads this statement which is not correct. How many statements have been attributed to eminent scholars, yet had no basis! Therefore it is obligatory to verify what is transmitted from scholars or non-scholars, especially, as I said to you just now, especially in this age in which desires have multiplied, partisanship has multiplied, and people have come to walk as if in blindness.

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty. But Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it appealing in your hearts⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 7]. As you know, this verse came after the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁ And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Hujurat 6, 7].

The cause of what preceded was that the Prophet ﷺ had been informed about some people concerning matters that were not in them, so Allah the Exalted commanded verifying reports when they are brought by one whose uprightness is not known. It seems that some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wanted the Prophet ﷺ to punish those about whom he had been informed, but the Prophet ﷺ did not do so after the verse was revealed: ﴿If a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾.

But the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, which is His words: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾, i.e., it would be hard upon you, what you request from the Messenger ﷺ.

There are many examples of this. Among them: the Prophet ﷺ once led his Companions in Ramadan in the night prayer; he departed when some of the night remained, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had extended for us the rest of our night" — i.e., they asked him to stand with them the whole night — but he ﷺ said to them: "Whoever stands with the imam until he departs, a night's standing is written for him,"[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (1375) and al-Tirmidhi (806) from Abu Dhar.]] and he did not agree with their request, because of the difficulty and hardship in it.

Among them: some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ inquired about his deeds in private — i.e., what was not apparent to people — which are the acts of worship he performed in his house, and they considered them little, and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been forgiven his past and future sins," meaning: as for us, that is not for us. One of them said: "I will fast and not break my fast." The second said: "I will stand and not sleep." The third said: "And I will not marry women." When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "As for me, I fast and break my fast, I stand and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401/5) from Anas ibn Malik.]] He thus warned them against doing deeds that would be hard for them.

Also among this is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that "it reached the Prophet ﷺ that he had said: 'I will fast the day and stand in prayer the night as long as I live.' The Prophet ﷺ summoned him and said: 'Did you say this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You cannot bear that.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1976) and Muslim (1159/181) from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr.]] Then he guided him to what was better and easier.

The summary: among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, there are those with lofty resolve, but the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, did not obey them in much of the matter, because that would have been hard upon them had he obeyed them.

Then He said: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾.

Someone may say: what is the connection between His words, ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, and His words, ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾?

The answer: you obey him — i.e., the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace — in what goes against your wishes, because Allah has endeared the faith to you, so you prefer obedience to the Prophet ﷺ in what contradicts you; because Allah has endeared the faith to you and made it appealing in your hearts. This is a corrective exception of the most eloquent kind; meaning: but if the Prophet ﷺ opposes you in much of what you want, you will not hate that, nor will you oppose him, nor will you bear ill will toward the Messenger ﷺ because of it. ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, i.e., made it beloved in your hearts, ﴿and made it appealing in your hearts﴾, meaning: He made you love it, and made it appealing in your hearts such that you do not abandon it after you have acted upon it. This is because a person's doing a thing out of love may be a passing love, but when the thing is made attractive to him, the love becomes firm and lasting. Therefore He said: ﴿endeared to you the faith﴾, and this is in the heart; and ﴿made it appealing in your hearts﴾ also in the heart. But when the beloved thing is made attractive to a person, he persists in it and remains steadfast upon it.

This is a descent from the highest to what is below it: disbelief is greater than defiance, and defiance is greater than disobedience. Disbelief is leaving Islam entirely, and it has well-known causes in the books of the scholars, which the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned in the chapter on the rulings of the apostate. As for defiance, it is less than disbelief, but it is the commission of a major sin: that a person commits a major sin and does not repent from it, such as adultery, drinking wine, theft, slander, and the like. Disobedience is below this, and disobedience means minor sins, which are expiated by good deeds, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, so long as major sins are avoided."[[Recorded by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah.]] So the sincere believers, Allah has endeared the faith to them, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to them. We ask Allah to make us among them.

﴿Those are the rightly guided⦁﴾. "Those" refers to those whom Allah has endeared the faith to, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to.

﴿Those are the rightly guided﴾, meaning: those who have taken the path of rectitude (rushd). Rushd in origin means good conduct, and it varies in each context. Rushd in wealth is that a person manages it well and does not spend it on what is not beneficial.

Rushd in guardianship of marriage, for example, is that the guardian knows what is suitable (kafa'ah) and the interests of the marriage.

Rushd in religion is steadfastness upon the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Those whom Allah has endeared the faith to and made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to, are the rightly guided.

And here you find all these actions attributed to Allah: He endeared — who? He made it appealing — Allah. He made hateful — Allah, Mighty and Majestic...

Thus He said after it: ﴿Grace from Allah﴾, meaning: Allah has bestowed upon you grace, that is, a favour from Him, and it is not by your own earning, but it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And so that it may be known that Allah, the Exalted, knows best where to place His message, and knows best where to place faith in a person. Whoever Allah knows to have good intention, good purpose and sincerity, faith is made beloved to him, He adorns it in his heart, and He makes disbelief, wickedness and disobedience hateful to him.
