So sins are a cause of opposition and disobedience. Those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour and blessed them with the blessing of religion are those who were granted success in the truth. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Grace from Allah and a blessing﴾, meaning: a bestowal of blessing from Him upon them.

Blessing is of two kinds: a blessing in this world and a blessing in the Hereafter.

As for the disbelievers, they are granted comfort in this world, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and luxury in which they were jubilant﴾ [al-Dukhan 25–27], meaning: enjoyment. So these, that is the disbelievers, have a blessing in this world, but in the Hereafter there awaits them punishment and curse, and we seek refuge with Allah.

As for the believer, he obtains both blessings, the blessing of this world and the blessing of the Hereafter, even if he is poor, sick, childless, or has no lineage; for he is in blessing, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl 97].

Here He said: ﴿Grace and blessing from Allah﴾. The intended blessing here is the blessing of religion, which is connected to the blessing of the Hereafter.

The summary regarding blessing is that there are two blessings: a general blessing for all creation – the disbeliever and the believer, the wicked and the obedient – and a specific blessing for the believer. This specific blessing is connected to the blessing of religion and of this world. As for the first, it is specific only to the blessing of this world, so that the proof may be established against the disbelievers.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. These are two of the names of Allah, which Allah always pairs together: knowledge and wisdom. He is All-Knowing of everything; Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Talaq 12], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman 34], and the Exalted said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am 59], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Ali 'Imran 5].

So the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, encompasses everything. When a person knows that the knowledge of Allah encompasses everything, even what he conceals in his heart, he fears, is awed, and flees to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He does not say a word that angers Allah, nor does he do an act that angers Allah, nor does he harbour a belief that angers Allah, for he knows that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that and nothing is hidden from Him.

As for the Wise, He is the possessor of perfect wisdom. Wisdom means that everything He decrees, may He be exalted, is in accordance with and conforms to the interests; there is nothing Allah decrees except that it is a great wisdom. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Far-reaching wisdom, but warnings do not avail﴾ [al-Qamar 5], and the Exalted said: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8], and the Exalted said: ﴿And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50]. This is the meaning of the Wise, that is, the possessor of perfect wisdom.

It has another meaning: the possessor of complete judgement. Allah, the Exalted, holds judgement, as He said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura 10], and the Exalted said: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Nisa' 59], and no one judges by his own desire: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to take us and you under His care with His mercy and pardon, and to make us among those who know and benefit from their knowledge; indeed, He is over all things competent.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The tale-bearer will not enter Paradise"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6056) and Muslim (105/169) from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.]] — i.e., one who carries tales. And it is authentically reported from him ﷺ that he passed by two graves being punished and said: "Indeed they are being punished, and they are not being punished for something great" — i.e., for a matter that was difficult for them — "as for one of them, he did not guard himself from urine" — or "did not purify himself from urine" or "did not clean himself of urine," [variant reports] — "and as for the other, he used to walk about with tale-bearing," walking among people carrying talk to others in order to spread discord among them. "Then he took a fresh palm frond, split it into two, and planted one on each grave." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, why have you done this?" He said: "Perhaps it will lighten their punishment as long as they do not dry out."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (216) and Muslim (292/111) from Ibn 'Abbas.]]

﴿lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁﴾. Among this kind is what is attributed to some scholars of fatwas which they never spoke at all, or they spoke the opposite of what is transmitted from them. Some people may understand a word of a scholar in a sense other than the scholar intended, and a person may ask a scholar a question which the scholar understands differently from what the questioner has in mind, and then he answers according to what he understood; then this man comes and spreads this statement which is not correct. How many statements have been attributed to eminent scholars, yet had no basis! Therefore it is obligatory to verify what is transmitted from scholars or non-scholars, especially, as I said to you just now, especially in this age in which desires have multiplied, partisanship has multiplied, and people have come to walk as if in blindness.

﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty. But Allah has endeared to you the faith and has made it appealing in your hearts⦁﴾ [al-Hujurat 7]. As you know, this verse came after the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if a deviator brings you a report, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful⦁ And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Hujurat 6, 7].

The cause of what preceded was that the Prophet ﷺ had been informed about some people concerning matters that were not in them, so Allah the Exalted commanded verifying reports when they are brought by one whose uprightness is not known. It seems that some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wanted the Prophet ﷺ to punish those about whom he had been informed, but the Prophet ﷺ did not do so after the verse was revealed: ﴿If a deviator brings you a report, verify it⦁﴾.

But the lesson lies in the generality of the wording, which is His words: ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾, i.e., it would be hard upon you, what you request from the Messenger ﷺ.

There are many examples of this. Among them: the Prophet ﷺ once led his Companions in Ramadan in the night prayer; he departed when some of the night remained, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, if only you had extended for us the rest of our night" — i.e., they asked him to stand with them the whole night — but he ﷺ said to them: "Whoever stands with the imam until he departs, a night's standing is written for him,"[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (1375) and al-Tirmidhi (806) from Abu Dhar.]] and he did not agree with their request, because of the difficulty and hardship in it.

Among them: some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ inquired about his deeds in private — i.e., what was not apparent to people — which are the acts of worship he performed in his house, and they considered them little, and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has been forgiven his past and future sins," meaning: as for us, that is not for us. One of them said: "I will fast and not break my fast." The second said: "I will stand and not sleep." The third said: "And I will not marry women." When this reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "As for me, I fast and break my fast, I stand and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5063) and Muslim (1401/5) from Anas ibn Malik.]] He thus warned them against doing deeds that would be hard for them.

Also among this is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that "it reached the Prophet ﷺ that he had said: 'I will fast the day and stand in prayer the night as long as I live.' The Prophet ﷺ summoned him and said: 'Did you say this?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You cannot bear that.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1976) and Muslim (1159/181) from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr.]] Then he guided him to what was better and easier.

The summary: among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, there are those with lofty resolve, but the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace, did not obey them in much of the matter, because that would have been hard upon them had he obeyed them.

Then He said: ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾.

Someone may say: what is the connection between His words, ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, and His words, ﴿And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty﴾?

The answer: you obey him — i.e., the Messenger, upon him be prayers and peace — in what goes against your wishes, because Allah has endeared the faith to you, so you prefer obedience to the Prophet ﷺ in what contradicts you; because Allah has endeared the faith to you and made it appealing in your hearts. This is a corrective exception of the most eloquent kind; meaning: but if the Prophet ﷺ opposes you in much of what you want, you will not hate that, nor will you oppose him, nor will you bear ill will toward the Messenger ﷺ because of it. ﴿But Allah has endeared to you the faith﴾, i.e., made it beloved in your hearts, ﴿and made it appealing in your hearts﴾, meaning: He made you love it, and made it appealing in your hearts such that you do not abandon it after you have acted upon it. This is because a person's doing a thing out of love may be a passing love, but when the thing is made attractive to him, the love becomes firm and lasting. Therefore He said: ﴿endeared to you the faith﴾, and this is in the heart; and ﴿made it appealing in your hearts﴾ also in the heart. But when the beloved thing is made attractive to a person, he persists in it and remains steadfast upon it.

﴿And He has made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to you﴾: He made hateful to you disbelief, which is the opposite of faith; defiance, which is the opposite of steadfastness; and disobedience, which is the opposite of perfection. This is a descent from the highest to what is below it: disbelief is greater than defiance, and defiance is greater than disobedience. Disbelief is leaving Islam entirely, and it has well-known causes in the books of the scholars, which the jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned in the chapter on the rulings of the apostate. As for defiance, it is less than disbelief, but it is the commission of a major sin: that a person commits a major sin and does not repent from it, such as adultery, drinking wine, theft, slander, and the like. Disobedience is below this, and disobedience means minor sins, which are expiated by good deeds, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, so long as major sins are avoided."[[Recorded by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah.]] So the sincere believers, Allah has endeared the faith to them, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to them. We ask Allah to make us among them.

﴿Those are the rightly guided⦁﴾. "Those" refers to those whom Allah has endeared the faith to, made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to.

﴿Those are the rightly guided﴾, meaning: those who have taken the path of rectitude (rushd). Rushd in origin means good conduct, and it varies in each context. Rushd in wealth is that a person manages it well and does not spend it on what is not beneficial.

Rushd in guardianship of marriage, for example, is that the guardian knows what is suitable (kafa'ah) and the interests of the marriage.

Rushd in religion is steadfastness upon the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Those whom Allah has endeared the faith to and made it appealing in their hearts, and made disbelief, defiance, and disobedience hateful to, are the rightly guided.

And here you find all these actions attributed to Allah: He endeared — who? He made it appealing — Allah. He made hateful — Allah, Mighty and Majestic...

Thus He said after it: ﴿Grace from Allah﴾, meaning: Allah has bestowed upon you grace, that is, a favour from Him, and it is not by your own earning, but it is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And so that it may be known that Allah, the Exalted, knows best where to place His message, and knows best where to place faith in a person. Whoever Allah knows to have good intention, good purpose and sincerity, faith is made beloved to him, He adorns it in his heart, and He makes disbelief, wickedness and disobedience hateful to him. And whoever Allah does not know to have that, then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5], and the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. So sins are a cause of opposition and disobedience. Those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour and blessed them with the blessing of religion are those who were granted success in the truth. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Grace from Allah and a blessing﴾, meaning: a bestowal of blessing from Him upon them.

Blessing is of two kinds: a blessing in this world and a blessing in the Hereafter.

As for the disbelievers, they are granted comfort in this world, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿How many gardens and springs they left behind, and crops and a noble station, and luxury in which they were jubilant﴾ [al-Dukhan 25–27], meaning: enjoyment. So these, that is the disbelievers, have a blessing in this world, but in the Hereafter there awaits them punishment and curse, and we seek refuge with Allah.

As for the believer, he obtains both blessings, the blessing of this world and the blessing of the Hereafter, even if he is poor, sick, childless, or has no lineage; for he is in blessing, due to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl 97].

Here He said: ﴿Grace and blessing from Allah﴾. The intended blessing here is the blessing of religion, which is connected to the blessing of the Hereafter.

The summary regarding blessing is that there are two blessings: a general blessing for all creation – the disbeliever and the believer, the wicked and the obedient – and a specific blessing for the believer. This specific blessing is connected to the blessing of religion and of this world. As for the first, it is specific only to the blessing of this world, so that the proof may be established against the disbelievers.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. These are two of the names of Allah, which Allah always pairs together: knowledge and wisdom. He is All-Knowing of everything; Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [al-Talaq 12], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾ [Luqman 34], and the Exalted said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. And not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor a grain within the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but that it is in a clear register﴾ [al-An'am 59], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Ali 'Imran 5].

So the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, encompasses everything. When a person knows that the knowledge of Allah encompasses everything, even what he conceals in his heart, he fears, is awed, and flees to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He does not say a word that angers Allah, nor does he do an act that angers Allah, nor does he harbour a belief that angers Allah, for he knows that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that and nothing is hidden from Him.

As for the Wise, He is the possessor of perfect wisdom. Wisdom means that everything He decrees, may He be exalted, is in accordance with and conforms to the interests; there is nothing Allah decrees except that it is a great wisdom. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Far-reaching wisdom, but warnings do not avail﴾ [al-Qamar 5], and the Exalted said: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [al-Tin 8], and the Exalted said: ﴿And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50]. This is the meaning of the Wise, that is, the possessor of perfect wisdom.

It has another meaning: the possessor of complete judgement. Allah, the Exalted, holds judgement, as He said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura 10], and the Exalted said: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Nisa' 59], and no one judges by his own desire: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they, from their reminder, are turning away﴾ [al-Mu'minun 71].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to take us and you under His care with His mercy and pardon, and to make us among those who know and benefit from their knowledge; indeed, He is over all things competent.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

In this session we discuss the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act equitably. Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably.﴾ [al-Hujurat 9].

﴿Ṭāʾifatān﴾ (two groups): its singular is ṭāʾifah, meaning a group of people.

His saying ﴿iqtatalū﴾ (they fought) is in the plural. He used the plural because the ṭāʾifah includes many individuals; therefore it is correct for the pronoun to refer back to the dual in the plural form, taking the meaning into account. Otherwise, the grammatical rule for the dual would require him to say: "And if two groups of the believers fought (iqtatalā)", so that the pronoun agrees with its referent; but it has returned to it according to its meaning.

Fighting between believers has multiple causes: either bloodshed that occurs between them, or tribal zealotry and a jahili call, or a dispute between them over boundaries, or other things. The point is that its causes are many. And "Satan has despaired of being worshipped in the Arabian Peninsula, but he is content with stirring up strife among you"[[Narrated by Muslim (2812/65) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah.]]. He stirs discord among them until some of them kill others. When fighting occurs, it is obligatory upon the other believers to make peace between them; for this reason He said: ﴿So make peace between them﴾, meaning: strive for reconciliation by every means, even if it requires paying money and one party giving up some of its right to the other. This is because reconciliation necessarily requires that one of the two parties relinquish some of what it wants of its full right; otherwise, reconciliation would not be achieved. For this reason, when Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And reconciliation is best﴾, He then said: ﴿And souls have been made present to stinginess﴾ [an-Nisa 128]: every person wants his statement to be carried out, so concession is necessary.

When we have made peace between them, He said: ﴿But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses﴾. That is: suppose that after the reconciliation one of the two groups returns to fight the other; here there is no reconciliation. What do we do with them? We fight the oppressing group ﴿until it returns to the command of Allah﴾, meaning: until it returns to Him. The command of Allah means His religion and His law.

So look at the first stage: reconciliation. If reconciliation is achieved and one of them oppresses the other, it becomes obligatory to support the oppressed party and fight alongside it against the aggressor: ﴿fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah﴾. If it returns, then it is obligatory to cease fighting against it. It is not permitted to finish off the wounded, nor to pursue the fleeing, nor to take captives of their offspring, nor to seize their property, because these are believers.

﴿And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice﴾: if it returns to the command of Allah after we have fought it, and it comes back and lays down arms, it becomes obligatory to make peace between them with justice.

This is different from the first reconciliation. The first reconciliation is by halting the fighting; this reconciliation is by compensation, meaning that we examine what was destroyed on each side, and then we equalize between them with justice. For example: if one of the two groups destroyed property worth one million riyals belonging to the other, and the second group destroyed property worth one million riyals belonging to the first, then what? The two groups are even and they cancel each other out. But if one of them destroyed property worth eight hundred thousand riyals of the other, and the other destroyed property worth one million, then the difference is two hundred thousand riyals, which we impose upon the group that destroyed property worth one million. For this reason He said: ﴿So make peace between them with justice﴾.

﴿And act equitably; indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾: ﴿act equitably﴾ is a command to act with equity, which means justice, and this is an emphasis on His saying: ﴿So make peace between them with justice﴾.

﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act equitably﴾: that is, He loves those who act justly. It has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Those who act equitably will be on pulpits of light at the right hand of Allah: those who act justly in their families and in what they are entrusted with of the affairs of the Muslims"[[Narrated by Muslim (1827/18) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]].

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat 10]. This is in the nature of a reason for His saying: ﴿so make peace between your two brothers﴾. That is: Allah has obligated us to reconcile the two warring groups, because the believers are brothers. The two warring groups are brothers, and we too are their brothers, even while they are fighting.

If someone says: Did the Prophet ﷺ not say: "Insulting a Muslim is grave sin (fusuq), and fighting him is disbelief (kufr)" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (48) and Muslim (64 / 116), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud], and a disbeliever is not a brother to a believer?

The answer is to say: the disbelief the Prophet ﷺ mentioned is a lesser disbelief (kufr duna kufr). Not everything the Shari'ah describes as disbelief is disbelief that expels from the religion. Here Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has explicitly stated that these two warring groups are our brothers, even though fighting a believer is disbelief. So it is said: this is a lesser disbelief. The Prophet ﷺ also said: "There are two qualities among people which are disbelief in them: slandering lineage, and wailing over the dead" [narrated by Muslim (67 / 121), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. It is well known that one who slanders lineage or the wailing woman is not declared a disbeliever in the major sense. This shows that disbelief in the Law of Allah, in the Book and in the Sunnah, is of two kinds: disbelief that takes one out of the religion (kufr mukhrij 'an al-millah), and disbelief that does not take one out of the religion.

﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers﴾ [al-Hujurat 10]. In this there is clear indication of the call to show kindness toward these two warring groups, by His saying: ﴿brothers, so make peace between your two brothers﴾, just as you reconcile between your two full brothers by lineage, so reconcile between your two brothers in faith.

﴿And fear Allah, that you may be shown mercy﴾ [al-Hujurat 10]. That is: fear Allah, Exalted, by doing what He has commanded you and leaving what He has forbidden you, for when you do this you have taken a shield against the punishment of Allah, and this is taqwa. Accordingly, whenever you hear the word taqwa in the Qur'an, its meaning is: taking a shield against the punishment of Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

﴿that you may be shown mercy﴾: that is, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may have mercy upon you if you fear Him.

Here we ask, regarding what we have just said: how can He say: ﴿Indeed, the believers are but brothers, so make peace between your two brothers﴾ when the Messenger ﷺ said: "Insulting a Muslim is grave sin, and fighting him is disbelief"?

* Student: We say: the disbelief the Prophet ﷺ mentioned is a lesser disbelief, not the Prophet ﷺ intending the word kufr to mean the disbelief that expels from the religion.

* The Shaykh: You have done well, may Allah bless you. We say: a lesser disbelief, not the disbelief that expels from the religion. And with this the evidences are reconciled and do not contradict. (...)

Let us continue with what we began regarding the verse of Surat al-Hujurat, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them; nor let [some] women ridicule [other] women, perhaps they may be better than them﴾ [al-Hujurat 11].

As has already been mentioned, sukhriyyah (ridicule) is contempt and belittling. And His saying: ﴿perhaps they may be better than them﴾ and ﴿better than them﴾ means: in the sight of Allah, or in the future, or in reality. That is, if a man ridicules another, this person being ridiculed may be better than the one ridiculing in the sight of Allah, and may at the same time be better than him, and may in the future be better than him.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ [al-Hujurat 11]. Al-lamz (defaming) is faultfinding, such as saying: "So-and-so is dull-witted, so-and-so is tall, so-and-so is short, so-and-so is black, so-and-so is red," and whatever is similar to that which is regarded as a fault.

And His saying: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ has been interpreted in two meanings. The first meaning: do not let some of you defame others, because each of us is in the position of one's own self; your brother is in the position of your own self, so when you defame him, it is as if you defamed yourself.

It was also said that the meaning is: do not defame your brother, for when you defame him, he defames you, so your defaming him is a cause of his defaming you, and in that case you are as if you had defamed yourself. In this regard is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah curses the one who curses his parents." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can a man curse his parents?" He said: "He curses the father of a man, and he curses his father; he curses his mother, and he curses his mother." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5973), and Muslim (90 / 146), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]

In any case, the verse contains the prohibition of believers finding fault with one another. It is not permissible for you to find fault with your brother regarding a physical attribute or a moral attribute.

As for a physical attribute that relates to one's creation, your faulting him for it is in reality a fault against his Creator, Mighty and Majestic. Who created the human being? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Who made him with this attribute? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Can a person perfect his own creation, so that the tall becomes short, or the short becomes tall, or the ugly becomes beautiful, or the beautiful becomes ugly? This is impossible. So when you defame a person and find fault with him in his creation, you have in reality found fault with the Creator. Is this not so?

Therefore, if we found a wall built leaning, and we found fault with the wall, is our fault directed at the wall or at its builder? At its builder. Accordingly, if you find fault with a person in his creation, it is as if you have found fault with the Creator, Mighty and Majestic. So the matter is grave.

As for faulting him in his character, such as this man being quick-tempered, severely vengeful, or foul-tongued, then do not find fault with him, for perhaps if you find fault with him, Allah will afflict you with the same fault. This is why it came in a report: "Do not show gloating over your brother, lest Allah grant him well-being and afflict you" [related by al-Tirmidhi (2506), and al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (127), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa']. However, if you find in him bad character, then the obligation is sincere advice: you contact him if you are able to contact him, and you explain to him the fault he has, or you write him a letter, under your name or under the name of an advisor, for example.

﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames﴾ [al-Hujurat 11]. That is: let none of you insult another by a nickname, such as saying to him: "O corrupt one! O sinner! O disbelEver! O drinker of wine! O thief! O fornicator!" Do not do this, for if you insult him with a nickname, then either the nickname applies to him or it does not. If it applies to him, you have committed this prohibition; and if it does not apply to him, then you have slandered him and committed the prohibition also.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Wretched is the name of defiance after faith﴾ [al-Hujurat 11]. That is: it is wretched for you to move from the description of faith to the description of defiance. When? When you commit what Allah has forbidden, you become defiant. A person who commits one of the major sins becomes a defiant one, and if he commits a minor sin and repeats it and persists in it, he becomes a defiant one. So do not make yourself, after faith, and after the perfection of faith, a defiant one. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Wretched is the name of defiance after faith﴾, because this sentence is an expressive sentence that conveys blame, and whatever conveys blame is undoubtedly forbidden.

* We have derived from this noble verse: the prohibition of ridicule, the prohibition of defaming others, and the prohibition of insulting one another by nicknames; and that whoever does such things is a defiant one after having been a believer. Defiance is not merely a description of the tongue that carries rulings. For example, the scholars said: a defiant person is not valid as a guardian over his daughter to marry her off. A defiant person who wishes to marry off his daughter may not marry her off. Who marries her off? Her brother, if she has a brother, may be her guardian; her paternal uncle, if she has no relatives, or if they fear her father if they marry her off, the judge marries her off.

A defiant person's testimony is not accepted, because Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, if a defiant person brings you news, verify it﴾ [al-Hujurat 6]. If he testifies before the judge to a right, the judge says: we do not accept it, because you are a defiant person.

A defiant person is not valid to lead people in prayer. A defiant person who openly displays his defiance, his call to prayer is not valid. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, all said this, although in some of these matters there is disagreement. But I say to you: the word "defiant" is not a light matter, so that a person says: "The matter is easy; instead of being a believer he becomes a defiant one." This is not correct. This is why Allah blamed it, saying: ﴿Wretched is the name of defiance after faith﴾ [al-Hujurat 11].

﴿And whoever does not repent, then they are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat 11]. That is: whoever does these things, and they are how many? Three. ﴿And whoever does not repent, then they are the wrongdoers﴾. The one who does not repent is a wrongdoer. And injustice, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Injustice will be darknesses on the Day of Resurrection" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2447), and Muslim (2579 / 57), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr]. When the believers on the Day of Resurrection have their light running before them and on their right, these wrongdoers have no light. So it is obligatory to beware of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden, for you, O servant, are a servant of Allah, obeying His command and refraining from His prohibition.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever does not repent﴾, if someone asks: what is the meaning of repentance? We say: repentance is returning to Allah from His disobedience to His obedience. If a person does not pray in congregation, what is his repentance? That he prays in congregation.

If a person has stolen property from another person, what is his repentance? That he returns the property to its owner.

If a person sold with deceit, meaning he cheated in the sale, what is his repentance? That he abandons deceit, and returns what he gained through the deceit to its owner. That is, for example, if he increased the price of the goods through deceit, then he must return the excess gained through deceit to the deceived man. If he does not know him, then he should give it in charity on his behalf. For example, these goods without deceit are worth ten, and with deceit they are twelve; the increase is how much? Two riyals.

So if he repents from the deceit, he must return the two riyals to the deceived man. If he does not know him, then he gives that amount in charity on his behalf.

The definition of repentance is what? Returning to Allah from His disobedience to His obedience. It has conditions. Repentance has conditions; that is, not everyone who says "I repent to Allah" is a repentant. There must be conditions:

The first condition: that he sincerely intends Allah in repentance. That is, his repentance is not motivated by fear of his father, fear of his eldest brother, fear of the authorities, or repenting so that it is said: "So-and-so is upright." No, he must be sincere to Allah; that is, the motive for his repentance must be seeking the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and attaining His honor. Sincerity is a condition in every act of worship.

The second: regret for what he did. Regretting means feeling grief and distress that this thing occurred from him.

The third: that he ceases the sin immediately. That is, he abandons it at once if it is a prohibited matter, and if it is an obligation, he hastens to perform it.

The fourth condition: that he resolves not to return to it in the future. That is, there should be in his heart a firm, resolute intention not to return to this sin in the future. If he repents while saying: "Perhaps I will be overcome and commit the sin," this repentant's repentance is not valid. He must resolve not to return in the future.

The fifth condition: that the repentance be before the doors are closed, for a time comes when the door of repentance is closed and is no longer accepted from a person. The door that closes to the repentant is general and specific.

The general: is the rising of the sun from its west. We now see the sun rise from where? From the east, and set in the west. A time will come when the sun rises from the west; it returns, and who makes it return? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If all creation gathered to return it, they would not return it. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, returns it, He whose command, when He wills a thing, is to say to it: "Be," and it is. This great sun returns when it sets, returning from its west. When the sun rises from its west, everyone on earth believes, all of them: the Jew, the Christian, the Buddhist, the communist, and others, all of them believe, because they see something clearly indicating the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. But will faith benefit them? No, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they await only that the angels come to them, or your Lord comes, or some of the signs of your Lord come? On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith﴾ [al-An'am 158].

The Prophet (ﷺ) explained His saying: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾ as the rising of the sun from its west. At that time repentance will not benefit, even though all people believe, but it will not benefit. Why? Because the door has been closed; the door is finished. When it is closed, how can people enter?

The specific door: is that death approaches the person. When death approaches a person, repentance does not benefit, because of the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says: "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [an-Nisa' 18]. It does not benefit; the door is closed, finished.

I ask you: does any of us know when he will die? Never. A person may die while at his desk, on his bed, or in his prayer, at any moment. If we know this and are certain of it, it is obligatory that we hasten to repentance, lest death come upon us suddenly and the door be closed. This is why repentance from one's sin is obligatory immediately.

O my brothers! A person does not know when he will die, so it is obligatory that he hasten to repentance to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says: "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [an-Nisa' 18]. This one has no repentance; this is a report from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

An actual event confirms this: when Allah drowned Pharaoh and his people, what did Pharaoh say during the drowning? He said: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims﴾ [Yunus 90]. He repented now, did he not? But when? When he saw death. So it was said to him: ﴿Now?! And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus 91]. So his repentance was not accepted, and Allah forbid.

So the conditions of repentance are how many? Five: sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; regret for what was done; ceasing the sin he was upon at once; resolving not to return; and fifth, that the repentance be before the doors are closed. Five conditions.

If someone asks: repentance between the servant and his Lord is clear; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rejoices greatly at the repentance of His servant. If you repent to your Lord (and I ask Allah to accept repentance from me and from you), Allah rejoices at this with a great joy, a joy a person cannot imagine. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of one of you" – or he said: "at the repentance of His servant" – "than one of you with his mount" – the mount is the camel – "which carried his food and drink, and he lost it, so he searched for it and did not find it, so he lay down under a tree waiting for death" – his strength weakened and he was exhausted, and he lay down awaiting death – "then while he was in that state, behold, his she-camel was there with its halter caught on the tree. He took hold of the halter and said: 'O Allah, You are my servant and I am Your lord'" – he intended to say: "O Allah, You are my Lord and I am Your servant" – "but he erred from the intensity of his joy" [related by Muslim (2744 / 3), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud]. Do you find any joy greater than this? Answer, O people.

* Students: No.

* The Shaykh: Because he rejoiced in life after having been on the brink of death, so there is no joy greater than that.

So the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, rejoices at the repentance of one of us more than this man's joy in his camel. If the sin is between you and Allah, the matter is easy. But the difficulty is when it is between you and people. If a person stole from someone and repented from the theft between himself and Allah, it is over; there is no sin upon him, no punishment, no amputation of the hand, nothing. But is this repentance sufficient to discharge the stolen property returned to its owner, or must the property be returned to its owner? It must be returned to its owner. But the problem is how I return it. Perhaps if he went to its owner and said: "I stole this property from you and have repented, and this is your property," perhaps he would seize him and raise the matter to the responsible authorities. Perhaps he would say: "You have now given me ten thousand, and what was stolen was twenty thousand, is that not so?" Perhaps he would say this, and the person remains in a predicament. What should he do? We say: he may look to a trustworthy friend of his and say: "O so-and-so, he stole such and such from so-and-so, and this theft, take it to him, and say to him: this is from a person whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted repentance, and he took it from you before, and here it has now reached you."

But this man whom he appoints must deliver the money to its owner, and he must be trusted by the owner of the property and be trustworthy to him, because if he were not trusted, the owner of the property would suspect him, saying: "You are the thief, and the stolen amount is more than that." But if he is known to be his friend and trustworthy, the owner believes and trusts him, so he should say: "O so-and-so, may Allah reward you with good, the matter is such and such." If that is not feasible, he may place it in an envelope and send it by express post, and write in it in handwriting that is unrecognizable, meaning that his handwriting is not known, saying: "This is money for you from a person who took it from you earlier, and who has repented to Allah," and that is all; his obligation is discharged. The main point is that repentance is necessary; this is why He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And whoever does not repent, then they are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat 11].

If the owner is unknown, for example, a person stole in his youth from a person he does not know, or after reaching maturity he stole from property whose owner he does not know, then how is repentance realized? By giving this property in charity, freeing himself from it, intending it for its owner, not for himself, but for its owner, and by that he is cleared.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant us repentance before the doors are closed, and to help us and you in remembering Him, thanking Him, and worshipping Him well.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 12 (part 1 of 2):

God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿O you who believe, avoid much of [what may be] suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin. And do not spy, and do not backbite one another﴾ [al-Hujurat 12].

Opening the address with ﴿O you who believe﴾ indicates care for what follows. For this reason it is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When you hear Allah say: ﴿O you who believe﴾, then pay attentive hearing to it, for it is either good that you are commanded to, or evil that you are forbidden from." [Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd wa'l-Raqa'iq (36), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] That is, or it is a report from which a lesson and admonition are drawn, as God, exalted is He, says: ﴿There is certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding﴾ [Yusuf 111].

Here God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿O you who believe, avoid much of [what may be] suspicion (al-zann)﴾. Al-zann (suspicion) is when a person has two possibilities, one of which is more probable than the other. Here God, exalted is He, said ﴿much of suspicion﴾ and did not say "avoid all suspicion," because suspicion is divided into two kinds:

The first kind: suspicion of good for a person. It is required that you think well of your brothers as long as they are deserving of that, namely the Muslim whose outward state is uprightness (al-'adalah). Such a person is to be thought well of and praised for what has appeared to us of his Islam and his deeds.

The second kind: suspicion of evil. This is forbidden with regard to a Muslim whose outward state is uprightness. It is not lawful for anyone to harbor evil suspicion about him, as the scholars have explicitly stated. They said, may God have mercy on them: it is forbidden to harbor evil suspicion about a Muslim whose outward state is uprightness.

The second [form]: evil suspicion about one for whom there is an indication (qarinah) that he is deserving of it. For this, there is no blame upon a person in harboring evil suspicion about him. For this reason, among the well-known proverbs in circulation is: "Be on guard against people by means of evil suspicion." But this is not absolute, as is known. What is intended is: be on guard against those people who are deserving of evil suspicion, and do not trust them.

The essential point is that a person must inevitably have some suspicion in his heart about someone among people, based on indications surrounding it: either signs appearing in his face, such as a frown and aversion to meeting him and the like, or from his conditions that the person knows of him, or from statements that come from him, so that one harbors evil suspicion about him. When an indication of its existence is present, there is no blame on the person for harboring evil suspicion.

If it is asked: which is more: the suspicion that is forbidden or the suspicion that is permitted?

We say: the permitted suspicion is more, because it includes a whole category of suspicion, namely suspicion of good, and it includes much of evil suspicion, because if there is no indication pointing to that evil suspicion, it is not permissible for a person to characterize himself by it or to hold this suspicion. For this reason He said ﴿much of suspicion﴾, and did not say "most suspicion," nor "all suspicion," but said ﴿much of suspicion﴾.

Then He said: ﴿indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾. This sentence may suggest that most suspicion is not sin, and this fully agrees with what we have explained and divided: that suspicion is of two kinds, suspicion of good and suspicion of evil, and then evil suspicion is not permissible except when an indication of its existence is present. Therefore He said: ﴿indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾. So what is the suspicion that is not sin? We say: it is suspicion of good, and evil suspicion for which an indication exists is also not sin, because suspicion of good is the basis, and evil suspicion for which an indication exists has also been supported by the indication.

﴿Indeed, some suspicion is sin, and do not spy, and do not backbite one another﴾ [al-Hujurat 12]. Tajassus (spying) is seeking out the faults of others.

That is, a person looks, eavesdrops, and listens, perhaps to hear something evil about his brother, or perhaps to see something bad in his brother. What befits a person is to turn away from the faults of people and not to be eager to discover them. For this reason it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Let no one report to me anything about anyone" — meaning anything that would give rise to evil suspicion of him — "for I love to come out to you while my chest is sound." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (4860) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] So a person should not spy, but should take people at their outward appearance, unless there is an indication pointing to the contrary of that outward appearance.

In this part of the verse there is another recitation: ﴿tahassasu﴾ (with ḥa). It was said: their meaning is one. It was also said: rather, each of them has a meaning, and tajassus is for a person to try to discover the fault himself, while tahassus is for him to seek it from others. He says to people, for example: "What do you say about so-and-so? What do you say about so-and-so?" Whereas tajassus is one who tries to know the faults himself.

On this basis, the two recitations clarify two meanings, both of which are things God has forbidden.

Tajassus: trying to discover the faults of people oneself. Tahassus: trying to discover the faults of people through others, as when he says, for instance, "What do you say about so-and-so?" or "Have you not heard about so-and-so?", seeking by that his faults, because of what this involves of occupying the soul with the faults of others, and the person having no concern except to discover faults. For this reason, whoever is afflicted with that — that is, with tajassus or tahassus — you will find him in reality constantly anxious in his life, preoccupied with the faults of people rather than his own faults, and not concerned about himself. This is found quite often among some people who go to so-and-so and to so-and-so: "What do you say about such-and-such? What do you say about such-and-such?" You find their time wasted without benefit, indeed wasted in harm, because what they have fallen into is disobedience to God, mighty and majestic. Are you an agent for God, mighty and majestic, searching for the faults of His servants? The intelligent person is the one who seeks out the faults of his own self, and looks at his own faults in order to correct them, not one who looks into the faults of others in order to spread them, God forbid. For this reason God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, those who like that immorality should be spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment﴾ [al-Nur 19].

In any case, these are etiquettes and guidance from God, mighty and majestic, toward virtuous character: characters commanded and characters forbidden.

﴿And do not backbite one another﴾. The Prophet ﷺ explained backbiting (ghibah) by his saying: "It is your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." [Narrated by Muslim (2589/70) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] This is an explanation from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and he is the most knowledgeable of people about the intended meaning of God, blessed and exalted, in His speech. "It is your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes," whether that concerns his physical make-up, his character, his conditions, his intellect, his intelligence, or other things. The essential point is that you mention him with what he dislikes: whether in his physical make-up, such as saying, "So-and-so is ugly and deformed; in you is such-and-such," seeking the faults of his body.

Or in his character: as by saying, "So-and-so is foolish, quick to anger, badly behaved," and the like.

Or in his inner make-up: such as saying, "So-and-so is dull, so-and-so does not understand, so-and-so has poor memory," and similar things. The Messenger of God ﷺ defined it by a clear and explicit definition: "Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes." They said: "O Messenger of God! What if what I say is in him?" He said: "If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him, and if what you say is not in him, you have slandered him." [Narrated by Muslim (2589/70) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.] That is, you have combined slander (buhtan) and backbiting.

On this basis, it is obligatory to refrain from mentioning people with what they dislike, whether that is in them or not in them; it is obligatory to refrain from this. Know that if you spread the faults of your brother, God will set upon you one who spreads your faults, ﴿a recompense in accordance [with their deeds]﴾ [al-Naba 26]. Do not think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do; rather, He will set upon them one who treats them in the same way they treat people.

However, if backbiting is for a benefit, there is no harm in it and no blame in it. For this reason, when Fatimah bint Qays came to the Messenger of God ﷺ consulting him about men who had proposed to her, he clarified the faults of those whom he saw as having a defect. Three men had proposed to her: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him, Abu Jahm ibn al-Harith, and Usamah ibn Zayd. The Prophet ﷺ said to her: "As for Mu'awiyah, he is a poor man with no wealth; as for Abu Jahm, he beats women. Marry Usamah ibn Zayd." [Narrated by Muslim (1480/36) from the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays.] So the Prophet ﷺ mentioned a fault in these two men for the sake of counsel and clarifying the truth, and this is without doubt not considered backbiting. For this reason, if someone comes to you consulting about dealing with a man, saying, "So-and-so wants to deal with me in sale, purchase, or rent," or about marrying one who has proposed to his daughter, or the like, and you know that there is a defect in him, then it is obligatory upon you to clarify that to him. You must clarify it, and this is not considered, as the common people say, "cutting off provision," but rather it is part of clarifying the truth. If you know that this man with whom he wants to deal in sale is procrastinating, a liar, and a deceiver, then say to him: "My brother! Do not sell to this one; he is a procrastinator, he is a deceiver, he is a liar; he may claim that the commodity has a defect when it has no defect, or he may claim to have been cheated when he has not been cheated," and the like, so that you do not fall into conflict and dispute with him.

Suppose a man comes consulting you about a person who has proposed to his daughter, and the person outwardly has uprightness, outward righteousness, and good character, but you know a blameworthy trait in him. Then it is obligatory upon you to clarify this; you must clarify it. For example, you know that this man is a liar, or you know that he smokes tobacco but denies it and does not make it known to people. You must clarify it. Say: "This man outwardly appears upright, of good character, and good, but in him is such-and-such a fault." Even if he is inclined to marry him, explain the fault to him; then he is afterward free to choose, because he will be entering with insight.

In any case: what is excepted from backbiting, which is mentioning a man with what he dislikes, is, what? 
* Student: If someone asks him, requests advice from him.
* The Shaykh: Only if it is in the manner of counsel. We have mentioned the evidence for this from the Sunnah. Is there evidence from the practice of the scholars? Yes, there is evidence. Refer to the books of biographical evaluation (kutub al-rijal), for example. You will find them saying, "So-and-so son of so-and-so has poor memory; so-and-so son of so-and-so is a liar; so-and-so son of so-and-so has such-and-such," mentioning what is disliked of his attributes as counsel for God and His Messenger. So if the purpose of mentioning your brother with what he dislikes is counsel, there is no harm.

Likewise, if the purpose of it is seeking redress and complaining, there is no harm in that, such as a man wronging you, and you go to someone who can remove that injustice and say: "So-and-so took my money, so-and-so denied my right," and the like; there is no harm. Hind bint 'Utbah came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining about her husband Abu Sufyan, saying: "He is a stingy man who does not give me what suffices me and my son." The Messenger of God ﷺ said to her: "Take what suffices you and your son in a reasonable manner." [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (5364) and Muslim (1714/7), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] So she mentioned a description that Abu Sufyan undoubtedly dislikes, but it is from the category of what? Answer.
* Students: Seeking redress and complaining.
* The Shaykh: From the category of seeking redress and complaining. God, exalted, has said in His Book: ﴿God does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾ [al-Nisa' 148]; that is: he may speak openly of evil speech to remove his injustice. But is such a thing permitted if the person's intention is to lighten the burden of sorrow and pain in his heart, by relating the situation that occurred to a friend of his, a friend who cannot remove this injustice but relieves him of it, or is it not permitted? The apparent ruling is that it is permitted, by the generality of God's saying: ﴿God does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾. This happens often: a person is often harmed and wronged by the denial or seizure of property or the like, so a man goes to his friend and says: "So-and-so said such-and-such about me, said such-and-such about me," wanting to cool what is in his heart of pain and anguish, or speaks about it with his children, his family, his wife, or the like. This is not a problem, because the wrongdoer has no sanctity with regard to whom? To the one who was wronged.

(...) We had reached in the commentary the words of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿And do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. And fear God; indeed, God is Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾ [al-Hujurat 12].

Piety (taqwa) is mentioned frequently in the Quran, and likewise in the Sunnah. So what is this taqwa that recurs so often in the Book of God and on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may blessings and peace be upon him and his family? It is a great word; it means protection from the punishment of God. By what is protection from the punishment of God achieved? It is achieved by two matters:

The first matter: complying with the commands of God, mighty and majestic, by a person saying, when he hears the command of God: "We hear and we obey," for this is the saying of the believers. God says: ﴿The only statement of the believers, when they are called to God and His Messenger to judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [al-Nur 51]. So let there be no hesitation in your heart. Do not say, "Why did He command such-and-such?" Say, "We hear and we obey." Do not say, "What is the difference between such-and-such and such-and-such?" That is, why does God command this and not that? For example, concerning camel meat the Prophet ﷺ commanded us to perform ablution after eating it [narrated by Muslim (360/97) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah]; for this reason eating camel meat nullifies ablution according to the preponderant view of the scholars. So do not say, "Why does He command us to perform ablution after eating camel meat and not command us to perform it after eating beef, although both are called a bodna?!" Do not say such things.

A menstruating woman is commanded to make up fasting, and is not commanded to make up prayer. Do not say, "Why does He command making up fasting but not prayer?" as a form of doubting; rather say, "We hear and we obey."

The second matter by which taqwa is achieved: avoiding what God has forbidden. When God forbids something, say: "We hear and we obey, and we avoid it," and do not say, "Why?" Reflect on the saying of God, mighty and majestic, concerning wine, gambling, stone idols, and divining arrows, where He says: ﴿O you who believe, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan wants only to cause enmity and hatred to occur among you through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 90-91]. Look at ﴿So will you not desist?﴾, that is: after this explanation and clarification, will you desist or not? This interrogative has the meaning of a command; that is: so desist. For this reason the Companions said: "We have desisted, we have desisted." So taqwa is achieved by what? By two matters:

The first: complying with the command of God, mighty and majestic, without hesitation.

The second: avoiding the prohibition of God, mighty and majestic, without hesitation. Say, "We hear and we obey"; this is the saying of the believers.

God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, God is Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾. These are two of God's names: the first is al-Tawwab (the Accepting of repentance), and the second is al-Rahim (the Merciful). Al-Tawwab here is an intensive form; the active participle from tāba is tā'ib, and tawwāb means abundance of repentance, and that He, mighty and majestic, is characterized by this attribute. The Lord, mighty and majestic, is abundant in accepting repentance because His servants are many; this is one reason. And because the sins a person commits are many; how often does a person commit sin and God accepts his repentance. For this reason He named Himself al-Tawwab.

And what is repentance? Repentance from the servant is that he transfers from disobedience to God to obedience to Him.

And repentance from God is that God accepts from the servant and replaces his evil deeds with good deeds.

So repentance from the servant is what?
* Student: Transition.
* The Shaykh: From what?

Student: From sin to (...).

Shaykh: Returning from sin to obedience. Repentance from Allah is His acceptance of this repentance from the servant and His replacing his evil deeds with good deeds, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden⦄ — up to His saying: ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan 70].

It may also be said that repentance from Allah refers to His enabling the servant to repent. So Allah, exalted is He, has two kinds of repentance toward the servant: a repentance meaning enabling him to repent, and a repentance meaning accepting the repentance. What is the evidence for this? The evidence is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until when the earth closed in on them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined them and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them [in forgiveness] that they might repent⦄. Read what follows it.

Student: ﴿that they might repent﴾ [at-Tawbah 118].

Shaykh: ﴿that they might repent⦄. How did He turn to them? "Liyatubu" means: He enabled them to repent, so they repented.

As for the other kind of repentance, which is the acceptance of the servant's repentance, it is like His saying: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons evil deeds﴾ [ash-Shura 25].

The servant's repentance requires conditions, since not every repentance is accepted. O my brothers, there must be conditions:

The first: sincerity of intention.

The second: remorse for the sin, humbling of the heart and shame before Allah, azza wa jall, and that a person feels he is a sinner in need of repentance and of a blessing from Allah, azza wa jall.

The third: giving up the sin, either by doing the obligation and making up for it if possible, or by giving up the prohibited act.

The fourth: resolve never to return to the sin again. If he gives it up and feels remorse, but in his intention, whenever the opportunity arises, he would return to the sin, then this repentance is not accepted.

The fifth condition: that it be within the time when repentance is accepted, because repentance has a time after which it is rejected, however much the servant repents. This time when repentance is not accepted is of two kinds: specific and general.

As for the specific: it is when the appointed term arrives, meaning when death is present; then there is no acceptance of repentance whatever. The evidence is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"⦄ [an-Nisa 18]. This person has no repentance after he has witnessed and seen the punishment; he says, "I repent now," and it does not benefit him.

If a person commits a prescribed punishment (hadd) in this world and is apprehended, and then repents after being overpowered, is the prescribed punishment lifted from him? No; because of His saying: ﴿except for those who repent before you have power over them⦄ [al-Ma'idah 34].

Likewise, when death is present and a person witnesses and sees it, repentance does not benefit him, due to the noble verse in Surat an-Nisa. This actually happened when Pharaoh repented after drowning overtook him. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims"⦄ [Yunus 90]. What was said to him?

Student: He was told: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed\u200b⦄ before.

Shaykh: ﴿disobeyed⦄.

Student: ﴿disobeyed⦄.

Shaykh: ﴿before⦄.

Student: ﴿before, and you were among the corrupters⦄.

Shaykh: ﴿the corrupters⦄. He was told: ﴿Now?⦄ meaning: now do you believe in what the Children of Israel believed? This does not benefit: ﴿And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters⦄ [Yunus 91].

The second, general: the time when it happens to the people at large, when it occurs or comes, then repentance is not accepted. This is when the sun rises from its west. The sun now keeps moving since Allah created it: it comes from the east and sets in the west. When Allah, azza wa jall, wills the end of this world, the matter will be reversed, and the sun will come from the west. When people see it, they will all believe, because they know that this universe has a Manager. Otherwise, who can bring the sun from the west? Can anyone? No. This is why Abraham said to the one who debated with him: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west⦄ [al-Baqarah 258], "so the one who disbelieved was confounded." But when all people see the sun after it has set and returned from the west, they will believe. Yet is this belief compelled or chosen?

Student: Compelled.

Shaykh: Compelled, because they have witnessed it. This is why Allah, azza wa jall, said: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before or earned good through its faith⦄ [al-An'am 158]. The intended "some of the signs" here is the rising of the sun from the west.

So repentance requires five conditions?

Student: Remorse.

Shaykh: The first is remorse for committing the sin. Good. And the second?

Student: Sincerity of intention to Allah, azza wa jall.

Shaykh: Sincerity of intention to Allah, azza wa jall: that a person does not intend by repentance to attain a rank, or to attain status, or to be praised by people. An example: a person known for wickedness and immorality, and it is announced that a mosque imam is needed, and it is known that no one is appointed as imam of a mosque except one who is upright. He became upright in order to—what?

Student: To become imam in the mosque.

Shaykh: This kind of repentance does not benefit him, because he did not make his intention sincere for Allah.

The third condition?

Student: Resolve.

Shaykh: No, before resolve, the stage of giving up the sin: this is by doing what is obligatory, if it can be made up, or replacing it if it cannot be made up and there is a replacement, or giving up the prohibited act if the sin is a prohibited action.

Now, if the sin concerns the right of a person, such as someone who stole money from another person. Stealing is forbidden. The man repented and felt remorse and resolved not to return. How is the repentance realized? The money must be returned to whom?

Student: To its owner.

Shaykh: To its owner, and repentance cannot be completed without this. If he says: "I fear that if I go to this man and give him the money, some harm will befall me regarding my reputation, and perhaps I will be imprisoned, and I have repented to Allah before being overpowered, so what is the situation?" Is it permissible for him to give it in charity on behalf of its owner?

The answer: No, because its owner is known. But if it were unknown, he says: "By Allah, I stole from people I have forgotten or whose whereabouts I do not know," then here he gives in charity what he stole on their behalf. But if it is known, he must send it. So what should he do? We say: he may give it to a person he trusts and say: "O so-and-so, I stole this money from so-and-so, and I have repented to Allah. Please give it to him, and tell him: this is money from a person you are owed by him, and he is now paying it." Is this possible? If not, he may send it by post, saying: "This is money from a person you are owed by him." In this case, it is known that you did not write your name, is that not so? And it is also not good to write it with your own pen, because a day may come upon him; write it with a machine that prints, such as a computer or other, and send it to him. This is if the right is financial, a person's right. But if the right is non-financial, such as when you backbited a person in a gathering or gatherings, how is repentance from this? Many scholars said: you must go to him and seek his forgiveness, otherwise his good deeds will be taken from your good deeds on the Day of Judgment. Go to him and say: "O so-and-so, forgive me."

Some scholars said: it is not obligatory to seek his forgiveness; rather, you seek forgiveness for him and praise him in the gatherings in which you used to backbite him, and good deeds remove evil deeds. There is a hadith: "The expiation for one whom you have backbitten is that you seek forgiveness for him." [Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (6368) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]

But there is a third, moderate opinion, and perhaps it is the correct one: he says: if the person you backbit has come to know of it, you must go to him and seek his forgiveness, because what is in his heart will not go away until you seek his forgiveness. But if he did not know, it suffices that you seek forgiveness for him and praise him in the gatherings in which you used to backbite him. And Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Whoever has a brother come to him to apologize should forgive him. But should he question him, saying: "You now ask me to pardon you, but what did you do to me?" That is, should he question him and find out what happened, or should he say: "You are forgiven, and that's the end of it"?

The better course: he should not question, because the other person may mention something great, and his own soul may be unable to pardon him. Is that not so? Perhaps when he says, "Forgive me," he asks, "What will you do with me?" and he says, "I did such and such and such," and it is something great, and his soul refuses to pardon, because the soul commands evil. So the better course is not to ask, not to say, "What did you do?" and to seek his reward from Allah, saying: this person came apologizing: ﴿So whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is upon Allah⦄ [ash-Shura 40]. And were it not that he is remorseful and repentant, and that it is hoped in the future that this backbiting will become good praise, he would say: "You are forgiven by me," and his reward is upon whom? Answer me, everyone.

Students: Upon Allah.

Shaykh: His reward is upon Allah. So now we have: regarding the one whose wrong was not money, must he go and seek forgiveness, or not? There are three opinions on the matter:

The first: he must go to him and seek his forgiveness.

The second: there is no need; rather, he seeks forgiveness for him and praises him in the places where he used to backbite him.

The third: a distinction, and this distinction is the choice of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is the truth. It is this: if the one backbitten knows, you must seek his forgiveness until what is in his heart goes away; and if he does not know, there is no need to seek his forgiveness. This applies to the one who backbit another.

As for the one who was backbitten and asked for forgiveness, what we see is that the better and more perfect course is that he forgive him, because his brother came to him apologizing and remorseful, so let him pardon him. Be assured that if he pardons him, it will be a great and tremendous thing for that person; he will see that he has given him the greatest gift, and the dislike that existed before will turn into what? Love, affection, and harmony. This is what is required of Muslims: that some of them be companionable, loving, and affectionate toward one another.

Allah, azza wa jall, says: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful⦄. He, glorified and exalted, is Merciful, and He is Rahman, and the two names have been combined in the greatest surah in the Book of Allah. What is it?

Student: Al-Fatihah.

Shaykh: Al-Fatihah: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful⦄ [al-Fatihah 1]. The scholars said: when al-Rahman is mentioned alone, as in His saying: ﴿It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son⦄ [Maryam 92], and as in His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"⦄ [al-Furqan 60], or when al-Rahim is mentioned alone, as in this verse ﴿Accepting of repentance, Merciful⦄, their meaning is one: al-Rahim is the one of vast, all-encompassing mercy, and al-Rahman, when mentioned alone, is likewise the one of vast, all-encompassing mercy.

But when they are combined, al-Rahman is in respect of attribute, and al-Rahim is in respect of act. That is, He, azza wa jall, possesses vast mercy, and He is also merciful, continuously extending mercy to whomever He wills of His servants, as He, exalted, said: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned⦄ [al-'Ankabut 21]. I ask Allah, exalted is He, to encompass me and you, and all our Muslim brothers, with His mercy, and to make us among the callers to good and reform; indeed, He is over all things Competent. (...).

We discuss here the words of Allah, blessed and exalted, in Surah al-Hujurat: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another﴾ [al-Hujurat 13].

The address here opens with calling out to mankind in general: ﴿O mankind﴾, although the beginning of the surah addressed those who believe. The reason is that the address in the verse we are discussing is directed to every human being, since boasting of lineage and noble descent occurs among everyone. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O mankind﴾, and the address is to the believer and the disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked.

﴿Indeed, We have created you from male and female﴾. ﴿From male﴾ is Adam, and ﴿female﴾ is Eve. This is the well-known view among the scholars of tafsir (Quranic exegesis). Some of them held that what is meant by male and female here is the category, meaning that the children of Adam were created from this category: male and female.

In the verse there is evidence that a human being is formed from his father and mother, that is, he is created from the mother and the father. This is not contradicted by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿So let man consider from what he was created. He was created from a fluid, ejected, that issues from between the backbone and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq 5-7]. This is because if we say that what is meant by the backbone is the man's backbone and the ribs are the woman's ribs, there is no difficulty. And if we take the preponderant view, that the backbone and the ribs are attributes of the man, since the ejected fluid is the man's fluid, while the woman's fluid is not ejected, then man is created from the man's fluid. But the man's fluid alone is not sufficient. It must join with the ovum that the woman's womb produces, so this pairs with that, and the human being is created from both together, that is, from his father and his mother.

﴿We created you from male and female﴾. So, male and female: it is possible that what is meant by them is two specific persons, and who are they? Adam and Eve. Or that what is meant is the category.

That is, the male among the children of Adam and the female among the children of Adam. On this interpretation, the second one, there is a difficulty, because Allah mentioned in other verses that man was created from an ejected fluid, which is the man's fluid.

The answer to this is that it is said: this ejected fluid cannot by itself form the embryo, but it must join with the ovum that the woman's womb produces, and then the human being is created from male and female.

﴿And We made you peoples﴾ [al-Hujurat 13]: that is, We made you peoples and tribes. Allah made the children of Adam into peoples, and these are the roots of the tribes.

﴿And tribes﴾ are what comes below the peoples. For example, the Banu Tamim are considered a people, and the branches of the Banu Tamim that stem from the origin are called tribes. ﴿And We made you peoples and tribes﴾.

What is the wisdom? Is the wisdom in this making that people boast over one another, so that this man says: I am from Quraysh, and that one says: I am from Tamim, and this one says: I am from such-and-such, I am from such-and-such?

No, that is not what is meant. What is meant is recognition, that people should know one another. For if it were not for this which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ordained, a person would not know from which tribe he is.
