For this reason, claiming to belong to other than one's father is among the major sins, because when a person attributes himself to other than his father, he changes this natural disposition (fitrah) upon which Allah created people, namely that they are peoples and tribes for the sake of recognition. It is said: this is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, back to the ancestor who was the father of the tribe.

﴿That you may know one another﴾, that is, not that you may boast of lineage and noble descent.

﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat 13]. Nobility does not lie in a person being from such-and-such a tribe or such-and-such a people. Nobility is piety (taqwa). And true nobility that is genuinely noble is only nobility in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. A person's nobility among his own kind is nobility without doubt, and a person is praised for it if he seeks thereby the face of Allah. But the true, beneficial nobility is nobility in the sight of whom? In the sight of Allah. And by what does it come about? By piety. The more a person is God-conscious, the more noble he is in the sight of Allah. So if you wish to be noble in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then hold to piety, hold to the piety of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. In it is all good, all blessing, all happiness in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those who believed and were fearing Allah﴾ [Yunus 62-63].

How often does the word taqwa reach our ears! So what is taqwa? Is it a word that runs across the tongues and passes through the ears? No. It must be a word that is great, revered, magnified and respected.

Taqwa is that you carry out the obedience of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is taqwa. Examine yourself: are you upholding obedience to Allah? Then you are God-conscious. Are you opposing it? Then you are not God-conscious. A person loses from taqwa in proportion to how much he opposes the command of Allah and His Messenger.

Taqwa, then, is obedience to Allah by performing what He commands and avoiding what He forbids. So if we see a person who goes forward to the mosque, prays with the congregation, is humble in his prayer and performs it with every excellence, and another who, on the contrary, prays at home and limits his prayer to the obligatory, which of them is more God-conscious? The first is more God-conscious.

So he is nearer to Allah, even if he is a freedman, or the freedman of a freedman, while the other is of the highest lineage. For the one most God-conscious is the most noble in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Every person loves to be favoured by the ruler in this world and to be the nearest of people to him. So how is it that we do not love to be the nearest of people to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the most noble of them in His sight? The matter is desire and Satan; otherwise the matter would be clear.

Hold to the taqwa of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so that you may attain nobility in the sight of Allah. We seek the forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him.

﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [al-Hujurat 13]: all-knowing of everything, because the word here is unrestricted and is not limited to any circumstance.

﴿Khabir﴾ (Acquainted), and khibrah (acquaintance) is knowledge of inner realities. Knowledge of outward matters is without doubt a quality of praise and perfection, but knowledge of inner matters is more far-reaching. So He is Knowing of the outward and Acquainted with what? With the inward. When knowledge and acquaintance combine, this becomes more comprehensive in encompassing.

It may also be said that khibrah has a meaning beyond knowledge, because the khabir among people is one who knows a thing and is skilful in it, unlike the person who has knowledge only but no skill, who is not called khabir. So on this view, the khabir includes a meaning beyond knowledge.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The bedouins say: We have believed﴾ [al-Hujurat 14].

Who is most God-conscious in the sight of Allah? Who is most noble in the sight of Allah?

* Student: The most God-conscious.

* Shaykh: The evidence?

* Student: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 14:

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed."﴾ Al-A'rab (the Bedouins): a collective noun whose singular is (a'rabi), and the a'rabi is a dweller of the desert, exactly like the badawi. The Bedouins boasted and said: "We have believed, we have believed," boasting of their faith.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: You have not believed; rather say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat 14]. It has been said that these were among the hypocrites, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾ [al-Tawbah 101]. The hypocrite is a Muslim, but he is not a believer; he is a Muslim because he submits outwardly, for the state of the hypocrite is that he is like the Muslims. This is why the Prophet (ﷺ) did not kill them, despite his knowledge of their hypocrisy, because they were outwardly Muslims who did not oppose. ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ [al-Baqarah 14].

It has also been said that they were Bedouins who were not hypocrites, but whose faith was weak: they walk with the people in the outward appearances of the Shari'ah, but their hearts are weak and their faith is weak.

So according to the first view, His saying ﴿and faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾ [al-Hujurat 14] means that it has not entered at all. This is according to the view that they were, what? Hypocrites.

And according to the second view, it means: faith has not yet entered in its complete and absolute sense; there is faith among them, but faith has not reached their hearts in its perfect form.

The rule we follow in tafsir is: when a verse admits of two meanings, it is to be understood as both of them together, so long as they do not contradict each other; if they contradict, a preponderant meaning must be sought.

﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed." Say: "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allah and His Messenger"﴾ [al-Hujurat 14]: meaning, outward obedience, upon which inward faith may be built.

﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾ ﴿He will not deprive you (lā yalitkum)﴾ means: He will not diminish anything of your deeds, because Allah the Exalted does not wrong anyone.

﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7, 8]. Whatever it is, it is fully repaid to the person. But glory be to Allah, His mercy precedes His wrath. ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 7], and will he be rewarded for it or not? Answer.

* Student: He will be rewarded for it.

* Shaykh: He will be rewarded for it. ﴿And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 8]. Will he be punished? He may be punished, and Allah may pardon him.

So evil deeds may be erased, but good deeds cannot be diminished. For this reason He said, after ﴿He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. The meaning of these two noble names has already passed, and we will limit ourselves to this extent, and what may be derived from this verse will come, God willing. (...)

Our meeting today opens with speech on the tafsir of the end of Surah al-Hujurat. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Bedouins say: "We have believed." Say: "You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts"﴾ [al-Hujurat 14]. We explained earlier that these people are a people in whom complete faith has not been realized; they possess the root of faith, so they said, "We have believed," and absolute faith is not given to one whose faith is not complete. This is why Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But say, "We have submitted," for faith has not yet entered your hearts﴾: that is, complete faith has not entered your hearts, but it is near, because (lamma) indicates the nearness of what follows it.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾; that is, if you carry out obedience to Allah and His Messenger by complying with the commands of Allah and His Messenger and avoiding the prohibitions of Allah and His Messenger, then Allah will not diminish anything of your deeds; He will give them to you complete, without deficiency. It is established that whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples; and that whoever brings an evil deed will be recompensed only with its like, and they will not be wronged.

Then the Almighty said: ﴿The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, then do not doubt﴾ [Al-Hujurat 15]. ﴿Innama﴾ (the particle of restriction) indicates the affirmation of the ruling for what is mentioned and its negation for everything else. That is: the believers are only these people. The meaning is that the true believers, whose faith is complete, are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿Amanu﴾ (they believed) means they affirmed with an affirmation that necessitates acceptance and submission. Mere verbal affirmation is not sufficient; acceptance and submission are necessary. The evidence that mere affirmation is not sufficient is that the Prophet ﷺ reported about his uncle Abu Talib that he is in the Fire [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6208) and Muslim (209 / 357), from the hadith of al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib.]], even though he believed in the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and affirmed him. He says in his famous lamiyya:

They have certainly known that our son is not a liar among us, nor is he one who is concerned with false speech.
And he says about the religion of the Messenger:

And I have certainly known that the religion of Muhammad is, among the religions of mankind, the best religion.
But he, may Allah protect us, did not accept this religion and did not submit to it, and the last thing he said was that he was upon polytheism, upon the creed of 'Abd al-Muttalib.
So those who believed in Allah and His Messenger are those who affirmed with a complete affirmation what Allah, the Almighty, deserves, and what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, deserves, and accepted that and submitted to it.

﴿Thumma lam yartabu﴾ (then did not doubt). The word ﴿thumma﴾ here is in one of the best positions. ﴿Thumma﴾ indicates sequence with a interval; that is: then they remained firm and steadfast upon faith over a long period. ﴿Lam yartabu﴾ means: doubt did not reach them concerning their faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Here we draw attention to a matter about which people frequently ask at this time, although its origin existed in the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: the whisperings (waswasa) that Satan casts into the heart of a person. Satan sometimes casts into a person's heart whisperings and doubts about faith: about the Qur'an, about the Messenger, about the Lord, the Almighty. These are whisperings that make a person wish his flesh were torn and his bones broken rather than speak of them. So what is the stance of a person towards this?

The stance of a person towards this is to seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan and stop. He turns away from this and does not think about it at all. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, reported that such whisperings are clear faith, that is, pure faith. This is clear faith because Satan does not come to a doubting person to make him doubt his religion; rather, he comes to a firm and steady person to make him doubt his religion and corrupt it for him. As for the believer in whose heart faith has settled and whose heart is at rest with faith, it is he whom Satan comes to corrupt. As for one who is not a believer, Satan does not bring him such whisperings, because he is already finished with him.

The important point is that His saying ﴿thumma lam yartabu﴾ indicates that they remained firm upon faith, even if the period was long. If someone says: What is the path that makes faith firm and stable for a person?

We say: First, that he reflects upon the creations of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and that these great creations were not the product of chance, nor did they come into being by themselves. Also, that he reflects upon the perfection of the Shari'a of Allah, and upon the biography of the Prophet ﷺ and his signs, and so on. Likewise, he should frequently remember Allah, the Almighty, for by the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest. He should also increase in acts of obedience and righteous deeds, because obedience and righteous deeds increase faith, as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunna wal-Jama'a, may Allah have mercy on them.

﴿And strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah﴾ [Al-Hujurat 15]. This is also conjoined to His saying ﴿amanu﴾. That is: they are those who, along with their faith in Allah, the Almighty, their certainty and their lack of doubt, wish to reform the servants of Allah. By what? By jihad in the way of Allah: they strive against the enemies of Allah so that they return to the religion of Allah and become upright upon it, not for revenge against them, nor to defend their own selves, but so that they enter the religion of Allah, the Almighty.

Jihad in the way of Allah is fighting so that the word of Allah is supreme, not for revenge. Fighting for revenge is nothing but defending oneself or taking vengeance only. But true jihad is that a person fights so that the word of Allah is supreme. As for fighting for the victory of the self, or merely in defence of the self, it is not in the way of Allah. Yet there is no doubt that whoever fights in defence of himself, if he is killed, he is a martyr, and if he kills his opponent, the opponent is in the Fire, as came in the hadith from the Prophet ﷺ concerning one who wanted to take your property. He said: «Do not give it to him». He said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if he fights me? He said: «Fight him». He said: What do you think if he kills me? He said: «Then you are a martyr». He said: What do you think if I kill him? He said: «Then he is in the Fire» [[Narrated by Muslim (140 / 225), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra.]].

So, what is jihad in the way of Allah? Fighting for what? So that the word of Allah is supreme. This is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, defined and distinguished with decisive clarity.

﴿Ula'ika hum al-sadiqun﴾ [Al-Hujurat 15]: those are the truthful ones in their faith and their lack of doubt. As for those Bedouins who said "We believe," but did not truly believe, rather they submitted, they are not truthful. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: You have not believed, but say: We have submitted﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 16:

﴿Say, "Will you inform Allah of your religion, while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth?"﴾ [al-Hujurat: 16]. This is a rebuke directed at those who said, "We have believed." The meaning is: Will you inform Allah, the Exalted, that you have believed, when He is All-Knowing of everything? The word ﴿tu'allimuna﴾ (you inform) here means "you tell Allah," and it does not mean "you remove His ignorance of your state," because He knows their state, the Mighty and Majestic, and He knows whether they are believers or not. Rather, ﴿tu'allimuna﴾ here means what? It means "you inform," not "you remove ignorance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic," because Allah is not ignorant of their state; rather, He is All-Knowing.

﴿Will you inform Allah of your religion﴾ when you say, "We have believed"? ﴿And Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, and among that, i.e., among what is in the heavens and the earth, is your state, whether you are believers or not.

* In this verse there is an indication that uttering the intention aloud in acts of worship is disapproved (munkar). This is because a person who says, "I want to pray," Allah, glorified and exalted, knows what action he intends, and Allah knows. Likewise the one who says, "I want to fast," and the one who says, "I intend to give charity," and the one who says, "I intend to perform Hajj," also. For this reason, it is not recommended to utter the intention in all acts of worship: not in Hajj, nor in charity, nor in fasting, nor in ablution, nor in prayer, nor otherwise. Why? Because the place of intention is the heart, and Allah knows that; there is no need to inform Allah of it.

﴿And Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾

﴿Whatever is in the heavens﴾ is general, and ﴿whatever is on the earth﴾ is general: everything Allah knows. We have already discussed this great attribute of Allah many times, which is among the broadest of His attributes, may He be exalted.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of everything﴾: ﴿of everything﴾, whether hidden or manifest, general or specific, He, may He be exalted, knows it.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17], up to the end of the verses, to the end of the surah. We will complete it, God willing, in the next session, since time has run out on us, and let us turn to the questions.

Accordingly, we say: we will speak, by what God Almighty makes easy, about the remainder of the tafsir of Surat al-Hujurat. God Almighty says to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿They think it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not count your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith.﴾

In this verse, "an" (أن) is repeated three times. ﴿They think it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not count your Islam as a favour to me. Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful.﴾ [al-Hujurat 17] It is repeated twice, and it is on the assumption of the preposition "ba'" (بـ); that is, they count it a favour to you, O Muhammad, by their Islam. This is the assumed reading, and the deletion of the preposition before "an" (أن) and "an" is regular, as Ibn Malik, may God have mercy on him, said in his Alfiyya. In the Khulasa he says, may God have mercy on him: the deletion of the preposition before "an" and "an" is regular, provided there is no ambiguity.

﴿They think it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam﴾, i.e., by their having embraced Islam. It refers to a people who embraced Islam without fighting, and so they began to count it a favour upon the Messenger ﷺ, citing their merits and saying: "We believed in you, and we did not fight you as the people fought you." Yet for whose benefit is it? It is for their own benefit. Therefore God the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith.﴾

His saying: ﴿Rather, God confers a favour upon you﴾ is a turning away (idrab, إضراب) to nullify what preceded; that is, you have no favour upon the Messenger ﷺ by your Islam. Rather, the favour belongs to God the Exalted upon you, that He has guided you to faith. There is no doubt that this is the greatest favour: that God the Exalted bestows upon a servant the guidance to faith, especially since God has misguided many of the community from it. Of the children of Adam, nine hundred and ninety-nine out of every thousand are in the Fire, and one out of a thousand is in Paradise. Whoever is granted success to be among the people of Paradise, that is a great favour from God upon him. Therefore the Ansar, may God be pleased with them, when the Prophet ﷺ gathered them on the day he divided the spoils of Hunayn, whenever he mentioned something to them, they would say: "God and His Messenger are more gracious." He said: "Did I not find you misguided, and God guided you through me?" They said: "God and His Messenger are more gracious." He said: "Did I not find you divided, and God united you through me?" They said: "God and His Messenger are more gracious."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4330), and Muslim (1061/139), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim.]] Whenever he mentioned something, they said: "God and His Messenger are more gracious." So the favour belongs to God upon us, upon everyone whom God has guided, upon everyone to whom God has granted a blessing; the favour belongs to God the Exalted upon him.

His saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾ means: if you are of those who possess truthfulness, those who speak the truth; so know this, that the favour is God's upon you.

﴿Rather, God confers a favour upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you are truthful.﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 49, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ [al-Hujurat: 18]. Allah informs us through this verse that He knows everything that is hidden in the heavens and the earth, and what is manifest is all the more so.

He, may He be exalted and glorified, also informs us that among the things He knows is the work of the children of Adam; for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. This verse conveys a great principle regarding a person's conduct and actions: that he should know that Allah, may He be exalted, sees his deeds and encompasses them, so that he fears Allah and guards himself against Him.

We ask Allah, exalted is He, to bestow upon us and upon you guidance and success.

How excellent it would be if one of you spoke on this surah, drew out the great etiquettes contained in it, and gathered them together so that they might serve as a reference for him when needed. I have seen some people compile a separate work on the etiquettes and moral conduct derived from these noble verses, and they are deserving of that.

We ask Allah to bestow upon us and upon you virtuous character and lofty manners; indeed, He is capable of all things.
